33	// Check verifies that the Antigravity CLI is available and returns its resolved
34	// location and version (`agy --version` prints a bare semver such as "1.0.2").
35	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
36		cmdName, _ := parseCommand(customCommand)
37		isCustom := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != ""
38		slog.Info("Check: verifying Antigravity CLI installation",
39			"command", cmdName, "customCommand", isCustom)
40	
41		resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
42		if err != nil {
43			slog.Info("Check: binary not found on PATH", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
44			msg := buildCheckErrorMessage("not_found", cmdName, isCustom, "")
45			trackCheckFailure(providerID, isCustom, cmdName, "", versionFlag, "", "not_found", err.Error())
46			return spi.CheckResult{Success: false, Location: "", ErrorMessage: msg}
47		}
48		slog.Info("Check: binary resolved", "command", cmdName, "resolved", resolved)
49	
50		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
51		cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
52		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
53		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
54		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
55			errorType := classifyCheckError(err)
56			stderrOutput := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
57			slog.Info("Check: version probe failed",
58				"resolved", resolved, "errorType", errorType, "stderr", stderrOutput, "error", err)
59			msg := buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, resolved, isCustom, stderrOutput)
60			trackCheckFailure(providerID, isCustom, cmdName, resolved, versionFlag, stderrOutput, errorType, err.Error())
61			return spi.CheckResult{Success: false, Location: resolved, ErrorMessage: msg}
62		}
63	
64		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
65		if version == "" {
66			version = "unknown"
67		}
68		slog.Info("Check: succeeded", "resolved", resolved, "version", version)
69		trackCheckSuccess(providerID, isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version, versionFlag)
70		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
71	}

190			if meta == nil {

192				continue
193			}
194			result = append(result, *meta)
195		}
196	
197		return result, nil
198	}
199	
200	// ExecAgentAndWatch executes the Antigravity CLI for the given project and
201	// watches for transcript updates.
202	func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
203		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: starting Antigravity CLI execution and monitoring",
204			"projectPath", projectPath,
205			"customCommand", customCommand,
206			"resumeSessionID", resumeSessionID,
207			"debugRaw", debugRaw,
208			"hasCallback", sessionCallback != nil)
209	
210		if sessionCallback == nil {
211			slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: no callback provided, running without watcher")
212			return ExecuteAntigravity(customCommand, resumeSessionID)
213		}
214	
215		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
216		defer cancel()
217	
218		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: launching session watcher in background")
219		watchErr := make(chan error, 1)
220		go func() {
221			watchErr <- watchSessions(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
222		}()
223	
224		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: executing Antigravity CLI", "command", customCommand)
225		err := ExecuteAntigravity(customCommand, resumeSessionID)
226		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: Antigravity CLI exited, stopping watcher", "execError", err)
227		cancel()
228	
229		if werr := <-watchErr; werr != nil && !errors.Is(werr, context.Canceled) {
230			slog.Warn("ExecAgentAndWatch: watcher stopped with error", "error", werr)
231		}
232	
233		if err != nil {
234			return fmt.Errorf("antigravity execution failed: %w", err)
235		}
236		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: complete")
237		return nil
238	}
239	
240	// WatchAgent monitors Antigravity CLI sessions for the given project and invokes
241	// sessionCallback for each new or updated session until ctx is canceled.
242	func (p *Provider) WatchAgent(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
243		slog.Info("WatchAgent: starting Antigravity CLI activity monitoring",
244			"projectPath", projectPath, "debugRaw", debugRaw)
245		if sessionCallback == nil {
246			return fmt.Errorf("session callback is required")
247		}
248		err := watchSessions(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
249		slog.Info("WatchAgent: watcher exited", "error", err)
250		return err
251	}

253	// --- helpers shared across the package ---
254	
255	func classifyCheckError(err error) string {
256		var execErr *exec.Error
257		var pathErr *os.PathError
258		switch {
259		case errors.As(err, &execErr) && execErr.Err == exec.ErrNotFound:
260			return "not_found"
261		case errors.As(err, &pathErr) && errors.Is(pathErr.Err, os.ErrPermission):
262			return "permission_denied"
263		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
264			return "permission_denied"
265		default:
266			return "version_failed"
267		}
268	}
269	
270	func buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType string, command string, isCustom bool, stderr string) string {
271		var builder strings.Builder
272		switch errorType {
273		case "not_found":
274			builder.WriteString("Antigravity CLI was not found.\n\n")
275			if isCustom {
276				builder.WriteString("• Verify the custom path you provided is executable.\n")
277				fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "• Provided command: %s\n", command)
278			} else {
279				builder.WriteString("• Install the Antigravity CLI and ensure `agy` is on your PATH.\n")
280				builder.WriteString("• Re-run `specstory check antigravity` after installation.\n")
281			}
282		case "permission_denied":
283			builder.WriteString("SpecStory cannot execute the Antigravity CLI due to permissions.\n\n")
284			fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "Try: chmod +x %s\n", command)
285		default:
286			builder.WriteString("`agy --version` failed.\n\n")
287			if stderr != "" {
288				builder.WriteString("Error output:\n")
289				builder.WriteString(stderr)
290				builder.WriteString("\n\n")
291			}
292			builder.WriteString("Run `agy --version` manually to diagnose, then retry.")
293		}
294		return builder.String()
295	}

115	// Get retrieves a provider by ID (case-insensitive)
116	func (r *Registry) Get(id string) (spi.Provider, error) {
117		r.ensureInitialized()
118		r.mu.RLock()
119		defer r.mu.RUnlock()
120	
121		// Case-insensitive lookup
122		for provID, provider := range r.providers {
123			if strings.EqualFold(provID, id) {
124				slog.Debug("Retrieved provider", "requested_id", id, "matched_id", provID, "name", provider.Name())
125				return provider, nil
126			}
127		}
128	
129		// Log available providers when lookup fails to aid debugging
130		availableIDs := make([]string, 0, len(r.providers))
131		for id := range r.providers {
132			availableIDs = append(availableIDs, id)
133		}
134		sort.Strings(availableIDs)
135	
136		slog.Warn("Provider not found",
137			"requested_id", id,
138			"available_providers", availableIDs)
139	
140		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provider '%s' not found", id)
141	}

180	// GetProviderList returns a formatted string listing all providers.
181	// Used for help text and error messages.
182	// The result is cached since providers are static for the lifetime of the process.
183	func (r *Registry) GetProviderList() string {
184		r.ensureInitialized()
185	
186		// Build the provider list only once and cache it
187		r.providerListOnce.Do(func() {
188			r.mu.RLock()
189			defer r.mu.RUnlock()
190	
191			if len(r.providers) == 0 {
192				r.providerListCache = "No providers registered"
193				return
194			}
195	
196			// Get sorted IDs for consistent ordering
197			ids := make([]string, 0, len(r.providers))
198			for id := range r.providers {
199				ids = append(ids, id)
200			}
201			sort.Strings(ids)
202	
203			// Build the formatted list by accessing providers directly (no Get() calls)
204			var parts []string
205			for _, id := range ids {
206				if provider, ok := r.providers[id]; ok {
207					parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", id, provider.Name()))
208				}
209			}
210	
211			r.providerListCache = strings.Join(parts, ", ")
212		})
213	
214		return r.providerListCache
215	}

11	// ErrReconstructionUnsupported is returned by a provider that carries the

13	// Reconstruction is on the Provider interface so every provider implements the
14	// method, but only some providers (initially Claude Code and Codex CLI) produce
15	// real native output.

18	// ReconstructOptions controls how a session is reconstructed into native form.
19	type ReconstructOptions struct {
20		// WorkspaceRoot is the target working directory the reconstructed session
21		// should belong to. Native paths/IDs are derived from it. When empty, the
22		// provider falls back to the SessionData's own WorkspaceRoot.
23		WorkspaceRoot string
24	
25		// MigrationNote, when set, is prepended as a leading agent turn so the agent
26		// understands the prior turns were imported from another session. Optional.
27		MigrationNote string
28	}
29	
30	// ReconstructedSession is the native output of reconstruction. It is data only;
31	// the caller decides where (and whether) to write it.
32	type ReconstructedSession struct {
33		SessionID string // freshly minted, native-format session ID
34		Filename  string // suggested native filename (base name, not a full path)
35		Content   []byte // native session file bytes
36	}
37	
38	// Turn is a single role-tagged text turn in the flattened transcript. The
39	// reconstruction model collapses everything an agent said, thought, or did into
40	// plain user/agent text turns (see docs/SESSION-PORTABILITY.md), which each
41	// provider then serializes into its native format.
42	type Turn struct {
43		Role string // schema.RoleUser or schema.RoleAgent
44		Text string
45	}
46	
47	// FlattenSessionData reduces a SessionData into an ordered list of plain
48	// user/agent text turns. This is the single place the cross-provider flattening
49	// policy lives, so every provider's serializer consumes the same transcript.
50	//
51	// Rules (per the locked design):
52	//   - user/agent text content -> a turn of that role
53	//   - thinking content -> folded into the agent turn's text (not dropped)
54	//   - tool calls -> folded into the agent turn's text via the pre-rendered
55	//     Summary / FormattedMarkdown captured on the forward pass
56	//   - model, usage, and path hints -> dropped
57	//
58	// migrationNote, when non-empty, becomes a leading agent turn.
59	func FlattenSessionData(data *schema.SessionData, migrationNote string) []Turn {
60		var turns []Turn
61	
62		if strings.TrimSpace(migrationNote) != "" {
63			turns = append(turns, Turn{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Text: strings.TrimSpace(migrationNote)})
64		}
65	
66		if data == nil {
67			return turns
68		}
69	
70		for i := range data.Exchanges {
71			for j := range data.Exchanges[i].Messages {
72				msg := &data.Exchanges[i].Messages[j]
73	
74				// Only user and agent roles produce turns; anything else is skipped.
75				if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser && msg.Role != schema.RoleAgent {
76					continue
77				}
78	
79				text := messageTurnText(msg)
80				if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" {
81					continue
82				}
83	
84				// Drop synthetic, non-conversational turns (slash-command invocations,
85				// local-command output, etc.) so they are not replayed into the resumed
86				// session. This is intentionally reconstruction-only — archival markdown
87				// stays faithful to the source session.
88				if isSyntheticTurnText(text) {
89					continue
90				}
91	
92				turns = append(turns, Turn{Role: msg.Role, Text: text})
93			}
94		}
95	
96		return turns
97	}
98	
99	// PrepareTurns validates session data and flattens it into the neutral turn list
100	// every provider's serializer consumes. It centralizes the two guards each
101	// ReconstructSession must apply before it can build native output: the source
102	// SessionData must be non-nil, and flattening must yield at least one turn.
103	// Keeping these here means every provider rejects the same cases with the same
104	// messages and cannot drift apart.
105	func PrepareTurns(data *schema.SessionData, opts ReconstructOptions) ([]Turn, error) {
106		if data == nil {
107			return nil, errors.New("cannot reconstruct nil session data")
108		}
109	
110		turns := FlattenSessionData(data, opts.MigrationNote)
111		if len(turns) == 0 {
112			return nil, errors.New("session has no content to reconstruct")
113		}
114	
115		return turns, nil
116	}
117	
118	// ResolveWorkspaceRoot picks the working directory a reconstructed session
119	// belongs to: the explicit target from opts when set, otherwise the source
120	// session's own recorded root. Providers derive native paths/IDs from the
121	// result; the cursor provider is the lone exception that needs no workspace.
122	func ResolveWorkspaceRoot(opts ReconstructOptions, data *schema.SessionData) string {
123		if opts.WorkspaceRoot != "" {
124			return opts.WorkspaceRoot
125		}
126		if data == nil {
127			return ""
128		}
129		return data.WorkspaceRoot
130	}

132	// reconstructMillisLayout is the RFC 3339 millisecond layout with a literal Z that the
133	// Claude Code, Codex, Droid, and Gemini serializers stamp on reconstructed records.
134	// (DeepSeek uses microsecond precision and formats its own.)
135	const reconstructMillisLayout = "2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z"
136	
137	// RFC3339Millis formats t with millisecond precision and a literal Z, the timestamp shape
138	// shared by the Claude/Codex/Droid/Gemini serializers. Callers pass a UTC time.
139	func RFC3339Millis(t time.Time) string {
140		return t.Format(reconstructMillisLayout)
141	}

144	// source slug, or "Resumed session" when the slug is blank or whitespace-only. Centralizing
145	// this keeps the trim (which a couple of serializers previously skipped) and the fallback
146	// consistent across providers.
147	func ResumedSessionTitle(slug string) string {
148		if title := strings.TrimSpace(slug); title != "" {
149			return title
150		}
151		return "Resumed session"
152	}

155	// most native session formats. Providers with a different role vocabulary (e.g. Gemini's

157	func ReconstructRole(role string) string {
158		if role == schema.RoleUser {

161		return "assistant"

172	var SyntheticCommandTags = []string{

175		"<command-args>",
176		"<local-command-stdout>",
177		"<local-command-stderr>",
178		"<local-command-caveat>",
179	}
180	
181	// extraSyntheticTurnMarkers are synthetic markers beyond the shared command tags
182	// that must also never be replayed into a resumed session: Claude Code's
183	// <TEXTBLOCK> title-generation wrapper and its interrupt marker (which also has a
184	// "…for tool use" variant, caught by the prefix).
185	var extraSyntheticTurnMarkers = []string{
186		"<TEXTBLOCK>",
187		"[Request interrupted by user",
188	}
189	
190	// isSyntheticTurnText reports whether a flattened turn is a synthetic,
191	// non-conversational artifact that should not be replayed into a resumed session.
192	// It matches by Contains because a flattened turn concatenates content parts, so a
193	// marker can appear anywhere in the text. Markdown generation does NOT use this
194	// filter and stays faithful to source.
195	func isSyntheticTurnText(text string) bool {
196		for _, marker := range SyntheticCommandTags {
197			if strings.Contains(text, marker) {
198				return true
199			}
200		}
201		for _, marker := range extraSyntheticTurnMarkers {
202			if strings.Contains(text, marker) {
203				return true
204			}
205		}
206		return false
207	}
208	
209	// messageTurnText flattens a single message into its turn text: all text/thinking
210	// content parts joined, followed by the tool's pre-rendered markdown when present.
211	func messageTurnText(msg *schema.Message) string {
212		var parts []string
213	
214		for _, part := range msg.Content {
215			// Both "text" and "thinking" parts carry their content in Text; thinking
216			// is intentionally treated as ordinary agent text.
217			if strings.TrimSpace(part.Text) != "" {
218				parts = append(parts, part.Text)
219			}
220		}
221	
222		text := strings.Join(parts, "\n\n")
223	
224		if msg.Tool != nil {
225			toolText := toolTurnText(msg.Tool)
226			if toolText != "" {
227				if text != "" {
228					text += "\n\n" + toolText
229				} else {
230					text = toolText
231				}
232			}
233		}
234	
235		return text
236	}
237	
238	// toolTurnText renders a tool call as agent text, reusing the markdown the
239	// forward pass already produced (Summary + FormattedMarkdown). Falls back to a
240	// minimal description when neither is available.
241	func toolTurnText(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
242		var b strings.Builder
243	
244		if tool.Summary != nil && strings.TrimSpace(*tool.Summary) != "" {
245			b.WriteString(strings.TrimSpace(*tool.Summary))
246		}
247	
248		if tool.FormattedMarkdown != nil && strings.TrimSpace(*tool.FormattedMarkdown) != "" {
249			if b.Len() > 0 {
250				b.WriteString("\n\n")
251			}
252			b.WriteString(strings.TrimRight(*tool.FormattedMarkdown, "\n"))
253		}
254	
255		if b.Len() == 0 {
256			// Nothing pre-rendered; emit a minimal, non-empty description so the tool
257			// activity is at least acknowledged in the transcript.
258			b.WriteString("Tool use: " + tool.Name)
259		}
260	
261		return b.String()
262	}

13	// GlobalSessionRef is a lightweight, project-discovering reference to a single
14	// native session, returned by Provider.ListAllAgentChatSessions.
15	//
16	// Unlike the project-scoped ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath), the project is NOT
17	// an input here: each ref carries the originating working directory (read from inside
18	// the session) so the caller — the `specstory reindex` command — can resolve project
19	// identity with utils.ComputeProjectID. The project is discovered, not supplied.
20	//
21	// It is intentionally metadata-only (no full SessionData parse); reindex re-fetches
22	// full data per ref via GetAgentChatSession(OriginCwd, SessionID) when it needs the
23	// conversation body. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
24	type GlobalSessionRef struct {
25		SessionID  string // native session id (uuid)
26		CreatedAt  string // ISO 8601 creation timestamp (first turn), may be empty
27		Slug       string // filename-safe slug derived from the first user message
28		Name       string // human-readable description (may be empty)
29		NativePath string // absolute path the provider opens to read this session
30		OriginCwd  string // working directory the session was launched from (-> project_id)
31	}
32	
33	// PathSessionReader is an OPTIONAL capability a Provider may implement: parse a single
34	// session directly from its already-known native file path, skipping the by-id discovery
35	// search that GetAgentChatSession performs.
36	//
37	// Why: some providers locate a session by scanning their native store. Codex's by-id
38	// lookup walks the entire ~/.codex/sessions tree on every call, so resolving N sessions
39	// that way is O(N²). reindex already holds each session's exact file path
40	// (GlobalSessionRef.NativePath) from enumeration, so a path-keyed parse turns that back
41	// into O(N). reindex prefers this when a provider implements it and the ref carries a
42	// NativePath, and falls back to GetAgentChatSession otherwise.
43	//
44	// originCwd is the session's originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd),
45	// passed through as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
46	// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath.
47	type PathSessionReader interface {
48		GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath string, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*AgentChatSession, error)
49	}
50	
51	// ScanReporter accumulates a provider's enumeration progress (sessions found) so the CLI can
52	// render a live "scanning" display. It is safe for concurrent use and safe to call on a nil
53	// receiver (a no-op), so providers can report unconditionally.
54	type ScanReporter struct {
55		found atomic.Int64
56	}
57	
58	// Add records that n more sessions have been found. Files that yield no session (warmup-only or
59	// sidechain-only transcripts) are deliberately not counted, so the running total reflects real
60	// sessions rather than raw files.
61	func (r *ScanReporter) Add(n int) {
62		if r != nil {
63			r.found.Add(int64(n))
64		}
65	}
66	
67	// Found returns the number of sessions found so far.
68	func (r *ScanReporter) Found() int64 {
69		if r == nil {
70			return 0
71		}
72		return r.found.Load()
73	}
74	
75	// ProgressEnumerator is an OPTIONAL Provider capability: enumerate all sessions while reporting
76	// scan progress into r (which may be nil — ScanReporter is nil-safe, so report unconditionally).
77	// Providers that don't implement it are enumerated via ListAllAgentChatSessions with no live
78	// feedback. reindex uses this to render a per-agent "Scanning agents…" display.
79	type ProgressEnumerator interface {
80		ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *ScanReporter) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error)
81	}
82	
83	// ScanSessionsInParallel walks root for *.jsonl session files and scans each one concurrently
84	// with scan, returning the collected refs. It is the shared engine behind each provider's
85	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress: providers differ only in where their sessions live (root)
86	// and how a single file's header maps to a GlobalSessionRef (scan).
87	//
88	// scan returns (ref, nil) to include a session, (nil, nil) to skip a non-session file
89	// (warmup-only / empty / sidechain-only), or (nil, err) to log-and-skip a malformed file.
90	// Files are independent and the per-file read+parse is CPU-bound, so scanning fans out across
91	// CPUs; output order is unspecified (reindex dedups and sorts later). r counts sessions found
92	// (not files scanned) and is nil-safe. label names the provider in scan-failure logs.
93	func ScanSessionsInParallel(root, label string, r *ScanReporter, scan func(path string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error)) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error) {
94		// Phase 1: collect file paths (dirents only — no opens).
95		var paths []string
96		walkErr := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
97			if err != nil {
98				return nil // skip unreadable entries rather than abort the whole sweep
99			}
100			if d.IsDir() || filepath.Ext(path) != ".jsonl" {
101				return nil
102			}
103			paths = append(paths, path)
104			return nil
105		})
106		if walkErr != nil {
107			return nil, fmt.Errorf("walking %s sessions: %w", label, walkErr)
108		}
109	
110		// Phase 2: scan headers in parallel. min(NumCPU, 12) is always ≥ 1, so no lower-bound guard.
111		workers := min(runtime.NumCPU(), 12)
112		pathCh := make(chan string, workers)
113		refs := make([]GlobalSessionRef, 0, len(paths))
114		var mu sync.Mutex
115		var wg sync.WaitGroup
116		for i := 0; i < workers; i++ {
117			wg.Add(1)
118			go func() {
119				defer wg.Done()
120				for path := range pathCh {
121					ref, scanErr := safeScan(scan, path)
122					if scanErr != nil {
123						slog.Warn("reindex: failed to scan session", "agent", label, "path", path, "error", scanErr)
124						continue
125					}
126					if ref == nil {
127						continue // not a session (warmup / empty / sidechain)
128					}
129					mu.Lock()
130					refs = append(refs, *ref)
131					mu.Unlock()
132					r.Add(1) // count sessions found, not files scanned
133				}
134			}()
135		}
136		for _, path := range paths {
137			pathCh <- path
138		}
139		close(pathCh)
140		wg.Wait()
141		return refs, nil
142	}
143	
144	// safeScan runs scan(path), converting a panic into an error so one malformed session file is
145	// logged and skipped (via the caller's normal error path) rather than crashing the whole sweep.
146	func safeScan(scan func(string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error), path string) (ref *GlobalSessionRef, err error) {
147		defer func() {
148			if r := recover(); r != nil {
149				ref, err = nil, fmt.Errorf("panic scanning session: %v", r)
150			}
151		}()
152		return scan(path)
153	}

17	// ReconstructSession rebuilds a Gemini CLI native chat session from the neutral
18	// SessionData so `gemini --resume <id>` can continue the conversation.
19	//
20	// Gemini stores a session as a single JSON document: a top-level object with
21	// `sessionId`/`projectHash`/`startTime`/`lastUpdated`/`kind` and a `messages`
22	// array. Each message is `{id, timestamp, type, content}` where a user message's
23	// content is `[{text}]` and a gemini message's content is a plain string. Tool
24	// calls and thinking are already flattened into agent text by FlattenSessionData,
25	// so reconstruction emits only `user`/`gemini` text messages. See
26	// docs/SESSION-PORTABILITY.md.
27	func (p *Provider) ReconstructSession(data *schema.SessionData, opts spi.ReconstructOptions) (*spi.ReconstructedSession, error) {
28		turns, err := spi.PrepareTurns(data, opts)
29		if err != nil {
30			return nil, err
31		}
32		cwd := spi.ResolveWorkspaceRoot(opts, data)
33	
34		newID := uuid.NewString()
35		base := time.Now().UTC()
36	
37		// Best-effort project hash; Gemini stores it but resume keys off the project dir.
38		projectHash, _ := HashProjectPath(cwd)
39	
40		messages := make([]map[string]interface{}, 0, len(turns))
41		for i, turn := range turns {
42			msg := map[string]interface{}{
43				"id":        uuid.NewString(),
44				"timestamp": spi.RFC3339Millis(base.Add(time.Duration(i) * time.Second)),
45			}
46			if turn.Role == schema.RoleUser {
47				msg["type"] = "user"
48				msg["content"] = []map[string]interface{}{{"text": turn.Text}}
49			} else {
50				msg["type"] = "gemini"
51				msg["content"] = turn.Text
52			}
53			messages = append(messages, msg)
54		}
55	
56		session := map[string]interface{}{
57			"sessionId":   newID,
58			"projectHash": projectHash,
59			"startTime":   spi.RFC3339Millis(base),
60			"lastUpdated": spi.RFC3339Millis(base.Add(time.Duration(len(turns)) * time.Second)),
61			"kind":        "main",
62			"messages":    messages,
63			// Provenance back-link to the source session this was reconstructed from, so the
64			// lineage stays traceable (matches claude/codex/droid). See docs/SESSION-PORTABILITY.md.
65			"specstorySourceSessionId": data.SessionID,
66		}
67	
68		var buf bytes.Buffer
69		enc := json.NewEncoder(&buf)
70		enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
71		enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
72		if err := enc.Encode(session); err != nil {
73			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to encode gemini session: %w", err)
74		}
75	
76		// Filename: session-<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM>-<first 8 of id>.json (Gemini convention).
77		filename := fmt.Sprintf("session-%s-%s.json", base.Format("2006-01-02T15-04"), newID[:8])
78	
79		return &spi.ReconstructedSession{
80			SessionID: newID,
81			Filename:  filename,
82			Content:   buf.Bytes(),
83		}, nil
84	}
85	
86	// NativeSessionPath returns where a reconstructed chat belongs in Gemini's store
87	// and, unlike the Claude/Codex resolvers, prepares the project directory: Gemini
88	// associates a tmp dir with a project via a `.project_root` marker, so for a
89	// project Gemini has never seen we create `~/.gemini/tmp/<name>/` with that marker
90	// and a `chats/` subdir. Returns `<projectDir>/chats/<filename>`.
91	func (p *Provider) NativeSessionPath(projectPath string, filename string) (string, error) {
92		if projectPath == "" {
93			var err error
94			projectPath, err = osGetwd()
95			if err != nil {
96				return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get current working directory: %w", err)
97			}
98		}
99	
100		// Reuse the project dir Gemini already associates with this project, if any.
101		dir, err := ResolveGeminiProjectDir(projectPath)
102		if err != nil {
103			dir, err = prepareGeminiProjectDir(projectPath)
104			if err != nil {
105				return "", err
106			}
107		}
108	
109		return filepath.Join(dir, "chats", filename), nil
110	}
111	
112	// prepareGeminiProjectDir creates a Gemini project directory for a project that
113	// Gemini has not seen yet: ~/.gemini/tmp/<basename>/ (falling back to the hash dir
114	// if that basename is taken by a different project), with a `.project_root` marker
115	// and a `chats/` subdirectory.
116	func prepareGeminiProjectDir(projectPath string) (string, error) {
117		tmpDir, err := GetGeminiTmpDir()
118		if err != nil {
119			return "", err
120		}
121		if err := os.MkdirAll(tmpDir, 0o755); err != nil {
122			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to create gemini tmp dir: %w", err)
123		}
124	
125		canonical := canonicalizeProjectPath(projectPath)
126		dir := filepath.Join(tmpDir, filepath.Base(projectPath))
127	
128		// If the basename dir exists but belongs to a different project, key off the hash instead.
129		if info, statErr := osStat(dir); statErr == nil && info.IsDir() && !matchesProjectRoot(dir, canonical) {
130			if dir, err = GetGeminiProjectDir(projectPath); err != nil {
131				return "", err
132			}
133		}
134	
135		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(dir, "chats"), 0o755); err != nil {
136			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to create gemini chats dir: %w", err)
137		}
138	
139		// Write the project-root marker so Gemini maps this dir to the project on resume.
140		rootFile := filepath.Join(dir, ".project_root")
141		if _, statErr := osStat(rootFile); os.IsNotExist(statErr) {
142			if err := os.WriteFile(rootFile, []byte(canonical), 0o644); err != nil {
143				return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to write gemini .project_root: %w", err)
144			}
145		}
146	
147		return dir, nil
148	}

```text
1	# Antigravity CLI — On-Disk Session Storage Format Spec
2	
3	Authoritative, reverse-engineered specification of how Google's **Antigravity
4	agentic coding CLI** (`agy` binary, version **1.0.2**) stores sessions on disk.
5	Intended for an engineer writing a Go parser. Every claim below is backed by
6	real captured data observed on macOS (Darwin 24.6.0).
7	
8	- App: `agy` on `PATH` (for example, `~/.local/bin/agy`)
9	- Version observed: `1.0.2` (via `agy --version`)
10	- App data root: `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/`
11	- Capture date: 2026-05-26
12	- Scenarios used for this spec (captured on disk at the time of analysis):
13	  - interactive TUI session, 11 steps, all `run_command`
14	  - `agy -p "say hello"`, 3 steps, no tools (text-only)
15	  - `agy -p` read+search without `--add-dir`, 80 steps, `run_command`/`list_dir`/`list_permissions`, has `RUNNING` + `SYSTEM_MESSAGE` + `ERROR`
16	  - `agy -p --add-dir`, file tools `view_file`/`write_to_file`/`grep_search`/`list_dir`
17	  - `agy -p --add-dir` edit + failing command, then `agy -c` continuation (multi-turn, append-only)
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 1. Directory layout
22	
23	```
24	~/.gemini/                                          # shared with Gemini CLI — DO NOT confuse
25	├── oauth_creds.json                                # OAuth creds (access_token, refresh_token, id_token, expiry_date, scope, token_type). Antigravity auth works off these even when CLI logs "not logged into Antigravity".
26	├── config/
27	│   └── projects/<projectId>.json                   # projectId(UUID) -> workspace path map  ★ project mapping
28	└── antigravity-cli/                                # ★ all Antigravity data lives here
29	    ├── history.jsonl                               # interactive-TUI prompt log (NOT print-mode) ★
30	    ├── installation_id                             # UUID string, no newline
31	    ├── settings.json                               # {enableTelemetry, model, trustedWorkspaces[]}
32	    ├── keybindings.json
33	    ├── last_check.timestamp                        # often empty
34	    ├── cache/onboarding.json
35	    ├── bin/{agentapi,webm_encoder}                 # helper binaries (agentapi is a 2-line sh shim)
36	    ├── updater/update.lock
37	    ├── knowledge/knowledge.lock
38	    ├── cli.log -> log/cli-YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.log      # symlink to latest log
39	    ├── log/cli-YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.log                 # klog-format server logs
40	    ├── conversations/<conversationId>.pb           # ENCRYPTED/high-entropy — NOT protobuf. IGNORE.
41	    ├── implicit/<uuid>.pb                           # ENCRYPTED/high-entropy. Different UUID namespace (NOT conversationId). IGNORE.
42	    ├── scratch/                                    # default workspace when no --add-dir given (see §5)
43	    └── brain/<conversationId>/                      # ★ one dir per conversation
44	        └── .system_generated/
45	            ├── logs/
46	            │   ├── transcript_full.jsonl           # ★ PRIMARY SOURCE — clean native-JSON tool args
47	            │   └── transcript.jsonl                # same steps, but tool-arg VALUES double-escaped (avoid)
48	            ├── messages/                            # internal system-message inbox (optional)
49	            │   ├── <messageId>.json                # one system message
50	            │   ├── read.json                       # {"<messageId>": true}
51	            │   └── cursor.json                     # {"last_read_unix_nano": <int>}
52	            └── tasks/                               # optional
53	                └── task-<N>.log                    # captured stdout of async (RUNNING) command N
54	```
55	
56	### Encryption confirmation
57	`conversations/*.pb` and `implicit/*.pb` are **encrypted, not parseable**. The
58	146 KB `conversations/<conversationId>.pb` has a gzip compression ratio of **1.00**
59	(incompressible) and `strings` yields only random 4-char fragments. `implicit`
60	files (200–600 B) gzip to >100% of original. **Both should be skipped entirely.**
61	The `.pb` extension is misleading — do not attempt protobuf decode.
62	
63	---
64	
65	## 2. Session identity & timing
66	
67	- **conversationId** is a UUIDv4. It names the `brain/<conversationId>/` dir AND
68	  the `conversations/<conversationId>.pb` file. This is the canonical session ID.
69	- There is **no top-level `conversationId` field inside the transcript files.** The
70	  ID is only the directory name. (It does appear embedded in the encrypted env
71	  var `ANTIGRAVITY_SOURCE_METADATA` that the CLI injects into child processes —
72	  see §3.4 — but not as a transcript field.)
73	- **createdAt** for a session = `created_at` of step_index 0 (the first
74	  `USER_INPUT`). There is no separate session-metadata file.
75	- **Per-step `created_at`** is RFC3339 **UTC** with `Z` suffix and **second**
76	  precision: `"2026-05-26T22:00:46Z"`. (The `messages/<id>.json` timestamps carry
77	  microsecond precision: `"2026-05-26T22:01:35.545540Z"`.)
78	- The user's local timezone is recoverable from the `<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>` block
79	  inside USER_INPUT content (e.g. `2026-05-26T18:00:46-04:00`).
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 3. Transcript schema (`transcript_full.jsonl`)
84	
85	One JSON object per line, ordered by `step_index`. **`transcript_full.jsonl` is
86	the file to parse.** Top-level keys observed (union across all sessions):
87	
88	| key | type | present on | notes |
89	|---|---|---|---|
90	| `step_index` | int | every step | monotonically increasing; has exactly ONE gap (see §4) |
91	| `source` | string | every step | enum, see §3.1 |
92	| `type` | string | every step | enum, see §3.2 |
93	| `status` | string | every step | enum, see §3.3 |
94	| `created_at` | string | every step | RFC3339 UTC `Z`, second precision |
95	| `content` | string | most steps | absent on bare tool-call steps that only carry `tool_calls` and on `CONVERSATION_HISTORY` |
96	| `tool_calls` | array | only on PLANNER_RESPONSE steps that invoke a tool | see §3.5 |
97	| `thinking` | string | some PLANNER_RESPONSE steps | model's private reasoning; may be absent |
98	
99	`transcript.jsonl` has the **same line count and same step structure**, but every
100	tool-call **arg value** is individually JSON-stringified (see §3.6). Prefer
101	`transcript_full.jsonl`; fall back to `transcript.jsonl` only if missing, and
102	then unwrap each arg value with a second JSON-decode.
103	
104	### 3.1 `source` enum (all observed values)
105	| value | meaning |
106	|---|---|
107	| `USER_EXPLICIT` | a real user message (the prompt) |
108	| `SYSTEM` | system-generated context/notice steps |
109	| `MODEL` | anything emitted by the model: its reasoning, tool calls, and tool results |
110	
111	Note: tool *results* carry `source: "MODEL"` (not SYSTEM), because they are
112	folded back into the model's turn.
113	
114	### 3.2 `type` enum (all observed values)
115	| type | source | role | `content` shape |
116	|---|---|---|---|
117	| `USER_INPUT` | USER_EXPLICIT | the user prompt | wrapped XML-ish blocks, see §3.7 |
118	| `CONVERSATION_HISTORY` | SYSTEM | turn-start context marker | **no `content` field** (empty placeholder) |
119	| `SYSTEM_MESSAGE` | SYSTEM | injected system notice (e.g. server restart, subagent stop) | `<SYSTEM_MESSAGE>...</SYSTEM_MESSAGE>` wrapper text, see §3.8 |
120	| `PLANNER_RESPONSE` | MODEL | model turn: text and/or `tool_calls` (+optional `thinking`) | the model's prose reply (may be empty when it's only a tool call) |
121	| `RUN_COMMAND` | MODEL | result of a `run_command` tool call | command output block, see §3.9 |
122	| `VIEW_FILE` | MODEL | result of a `view_file` tool call | line-numbered file dump, see §6 |
123	| `CODE_ACTION` | MODEL | result of `write_to_file` OR `replace_file_content` | creation note or unified diff, see §6 |
124	| `GREP_SEARCH` | MODEL | result of a `grep_search` tool call | JSON-lines of matches, see §6 |
125	| `LIST_DIRECTORY` | MODEL | result of a `list_dir` tool call | JSON-lines of entries + summary, see §6 |
126	| `GENERIC` | MODEL | result of tools without a dedicated type (e.g. `list_permissions`) | freeform text |
127	
128	The result step's `type` is derived from the tool category, NOT a single generic
129	"tool result" type. A `run_command` call produces a `RUN_COMMAND` result; a
130	`view_file` call produces a `VIEW_FILE` result; etc. Tools lacking a dedicated
131	type produce `GENERIC`.
132	
133	### 3.3 `status` enum (all observed values)
134	| value | meaning |
135	|---|---|
136	| `DONE` | step complete (the overwhelming majority) |
137	| `RUNNING` | an async / long-running command not yet finished at capture time (seen on `RUN_COMMAND` result steps where `WaitMsBeforeAsync` elapsed; its output later lands in `tasks/task-<N>.log`) |
138	| `ERROR` | step failed at the tool-execution layer (seen on `LIST_DIRECTORY` for a non-existent dir; content = `Encountered error in step execution: directory ... does not exist`) |
139	
140	**IMPORTANT — failed shell commands are NOT `ERROR`.** A `run_command` whose
141	process exits non-zero still has `status: "DONE"`; the failure is signalled only
142	in the `content` text: `"The command failed with exit code: 1"`. So to detect a
143	failed shell command, parse the content, not the status. `ERROR` status is
144	reserved for tool-framework-level failures (e.g. directory not found).
145	
146	### 3.4 Tool calls — `tool_calls` array
147	Present only on `PLANNER_RESPONSE` steps that invoke a tool. Each element:
148	```json
149	{"name":"<tool_name>","args":{ ... , "toolAction":"...","toolSummary":"..."}}
150	```
151	Every tool's args include human-readable `toolAction` and `toolSummary` strings.
152	Only **one tool call per PLANNER_RESPONSE** was observed across all sessions
153	(the planner emits one tool, gets its result in the next step, then plans
154	again). No parallel/multi-tool steps were seen, but parser should tolerate an
155	array of length >1.
156	
157	The corresponding **result** appears as the **immediately following step**
158	(`step_index + 1`, modulo the single gap at index 4 — see §4). There is no
159	explicit call→result ID field in the transcript; correlation is purely
160	positional (call at step N → result at next step). An internal tool-call `id`
161	(e.g. `"8bo3srsr"`) exists but is only visible inside the injected
162	`ANTIGRAVITY_SOURCE_METADATA` env var, not in transcript fields.
163	
164	### 3.5 Tool catalog (real args observed)
165	
166	| tool `name` | exact `args` keys (excl. `toolAction`/`toolSummary`) | result step `type` | result content shape | SpecStory tool type |
167	|---|---|---|---|---|
168	| `run_command` | `CommandLine` (str), `Cwd` (str, abs path), `WaitMsBeforeAsync` (int, e.g. 5000) | `RUN_COMMAND` | `Created At:`/`Completed At:` header + "The command completed successfully." or "The command failed with exit code: N" + `Output:`/`Stdout:`/`Stderr:` | **shell** |
169	| `view_file` | `AbsolutePath` (str) | `VIEW_FILE` | `File Path:` + `Total Lines`/`Total Bytes` + line-numbered body (`N: <line>`) | **read** |
170	| `write_to_file` | `CodeContent` (str, full file body), `Description` (str), `IsArtifact` (bool), `Overwrite` (bool), `TargetFile` (str abs path) | `CODE_ACTION` | `Created file file://... with requested content.` | **write** |
171	| `replace_file_content` | `TargetFile` (str), `TargetContent` (str, old text), `ReplacementContent` (str, new text), `StartLine` (int), `EndLine` (int), `Instruction` (str), `Description` (str), `AllowMultiple` (bool) | `CODE_ACTION` | `The following changes were made by the replace_file_content tool to: <path>` + unified diff between `[diff_block_start]`/`[diff_block_end]` markers | **write** (edit) |
172	| `grep_search` | `Query` (str), `SearchPath` (str), `MatchPerLine` (bool) | `GREP_SEARCH` | JSON-lines, one per match: `{"File":...,"LineNumber":N,"LineContent":...}` | **search** |
173	| `list_dir` | `DirectoryPath` (str) | `LIST_DIRECTORY` | JSON-lines per entry `{"name":...,"isDir":true}` or `{"name":...,"sizeBytes":"NN"}`, then `Summary: This directory contains X subdirectories and Y files.` (or `Empty directory`) | **read** |
174	| `list_permissions` | *(none beyond toolAction/toolSummary)* | `GENERIC` | bulleted list of permission grants | **generic** |
175	
176	Tools NOT exercised in capture but likely to exist (the planner referred to its
177	"search tool"/"file viewer" by capability, and the CLI has a sandbox/browser
178	subsystem): `codebase_search` (semantic search), browser/URL tools
179	(`execute_url`/`read_url` appear in `list_permissions` output), MCP tools
180	(`mcp(*)` permission), subagent/task tools. A parser should treat any unknown
181	tool `name` as **generic** and map by `type` of the following result step.
182	
183	### 3.6 `transcript.jsonl` double-escaping (the difference)
184	Same step at step_index 7 (`write_to_file`), both files:
185	
186	`transcript_full.jsonl` (native — USE THIS):
187	```json
188	{"CodeContent":"hi there\n","IsArtifact":false,"Overwrite":true,"TargetFile":"/tmp/.../greeting.txt", ...}
189	```
190	`transcript.jsonl` (each value re-stringified — booleans/ints become strings):
191	```json
192	{"CodeContent":"\"hi there\\n\"","IsArtifact":"false","Overwrite":"true","TargetFile":"\"/tmp/.../greeting.txt\"", ...}
193	```
194	Rule for `transcript.jsonl`: after parsing the line, each `args` value is itself
195	a JSON-encoded scalar — decode a second time (string→string, `"false"`→bool,
196	`"5000"`→int).
197	
198	### 3.7 USER_INPUT content structure
199	```
200	<USER_REQUEST>
201	<the real prompt text>
202	</USER_REQUEST>
203	<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>
204	The current local time is: 2026-05-26T17:58:35-04:00.
205	</ADDITIONAL_METADATA>
206	<USER_SETTINGS_CHANGE>
207	The user changed setting `Model Selection` from None to Gemini 3.5 Flash (High). ...
208	</USER_SETTINGS_CHANGE>
209	```
210	- **The real prompt is ONLY the text between `<USER_REQUEST>` and
211	  `</USER_REQUEST>`** (trim surrounding whitespace).
212	- `<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>` gives local time (timezone source).
213	- `<USER_SETTINGS_CHANGE>` is present only on the FIRST turn (model selection),
214	  absent on continuation turns. Filter both `<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>` and
215	  `<USER_SETTINGS_CHANGE>` out of the displayed prompt.
216	- The `model` chosen is recoverable from `<USER_SETTINGS_CHANGE>` ("Gemini 3.5
217	  Flash (High)") and also lives in `settings.json` `model`.
218	
219	### 3.8 SYSTEM_MESSAGE content
220	```
221	The following is a <SYSTEM_MESSAGE> not actually sent by the user. ...
222	<SYSTEM_MESSAGE>
223	[Message] timestamp=... sender=system priority=MESSAGE_PRIORITY_LOW content=[Notice] All your subagents ...
224	</SYSTEM_MESSAGE>
225	```
226	These mirror an entry in `messages/<messageId>.json` whose `recipient` is the
227	conversationId. Generally `hideFromUser: true` — treat as non-user-visible.
228	
229	### 3.9 RUN_COMMAND result content
230	Two observed shapes (the leading tabs are literal in the file):
231	Success:
232	```
233	Created At: 2026-05-26T21:31:15Z
234	Completed At: 2026-05-26T21:31:17Z
235	
236					The command completed successfully.
237					Output:
238					<stdout...>
239	```
240	Failure (note: status still `DONE`):
241	```
242	Created At: ...
243	Completed At: ...
244	
245					The command failed with exit code: 1
246					Output:
247					cat: nonexistent_file.xyz: No such file or directory
248	```
249	Some results use `Stdout:`/`Stderr:` sub-labels instead of `Output:` (seen when
250	both streams are empty). Strip leading tabs/whitespace when extracting output.
251	
252	---
253	
254	## 4. step_index semantics & the gap
255	
256	- `step_index` starts at **0** and increases by 1 per persisted step, with **one
257	  consistent exception: index 4 is always missing** in any session that makes at
258	  least one tool call.
259	- Pattern (verified across 4 tool-using sessions, all identical): `0,1,2,3,5,6,7,...`
260	  — i.e. exactly ONE skipped index, the slot right after the first tool's result
261	  (step 3). From index 5 onward the sequence is fully contiguous, even across
262	  later tool calls, system messages, and a continuation turn.
263	- A session with **no tool calls** (the text-only "say hello" session) has NO
264	  gap: steps `0,1,2`.
265	- **Interpretation:** index 4 is a reserved/hidden internal step the CLI emits
266	  once per session immediately after the first tool round-trip (most likely a
267	  hidden context/history refresh that mirrors the step-1 `CONVERSATION_HISTORY`
268	  but is not persisted to the transcript). It is NOT a sign of dropped data and
269	  NOT periodic.
270	- **Ordering is reliable.** Sort by `step_index` (equivalently, file line order —
271	  they already match). The gap at 4 should be ignored, not treated as missing
272	  content. Do not assume `result_index == call_index + 1` blindly across the gap:
273	  the first tool call is at step 2, its result at step 3, and the next planner
274	  step is 5 (4 skipped).
275	
276	---
277	
278	## 5. Project / workspace mapping  ★ (read carefully)
279	
280	This is the trickiest part because **the transcript contains no workspace field**
281	and `history.jsonl` does not cover print-mode sessions.
282	
283	### 5.1 What history.jsonl gives you (interactive TUI only)
284	`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/history.jsonl`, one line per user prompt typed in the
285	interactive TUI:
286	```json
287	{"display":"first prompt","timestamp":1779831073907,"workspace":"/path/to/project"}
288	{"display":"second prompt","timestamp":1779831156198,"workspace":"/path/to/project","conversationId":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"}
289	```
290	- `display` = the prompt text, `timestamp` = epoch ms, `workspace` = **absolute
291	  path** of the project (NOT symlink-resolved; it's the path as launched).
292	- `conversationId` is present from the **second** prompt onward; the FIRST prompt
293	  of a session lacks it (the session ID isn't assigned until the first turn
294	  completes). So to map prompt→workspace→conversationId, the conversationId on a
295	  line tags the session that the *previous* prompt(s) belong to.
296	- **CRITICAL LIMITATION:** `agy -p`/`--print` (non-interactive) sessions are
297	  **NOT written to history.jsonl**. Confirmed: after running multiple `-p`
298	  sessions, history.jsonl stayed at its original 2 (interactive) lines while 3
299	  new `brain/` dirs appeared. So history.jsonl maps only interactive sessions.
300	
301	### 5.2 Project configuration and CLI logs
302	`~/.gemini/config/projects/<projectId>.json`:
303	```json
304	{
305	  "id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002",
306	  "name": "/tmp",
307	  "projectResources": { "resources": [
308	    { "gitFolder": { "folderUri": "file:///tmp", "allowWrite": true } }
309	  ] }
310	}
311	```
312	- `name` and `gitFolder.folderUri` (`file://` URI) give the **workspace root
313	  path**. The `--add-dir /tmp/agy-recon-...` run resolved its project to
314	  `/tmp` (the git root), and the project id matched the
315	  `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` env var the CLI injected during that session.
316	- The path is the **git repository root** (an `--add-dir` of a subdir of `/tmp`
317	  mapped to project `/tmp`). It is absolute and appears NOT symlink-resolved.
318	
319	`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-*.log` can provide the missing practical
320	join while logs are retained:
321	```text
322	project: using project "/path/to/project" (id=00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002)
323	Conversation using project ID: 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002
324	Created conversation 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001
325	```
326	
327	The transcript/brain directory still has **no canonical metadata field** that
328	links `conversationId` to `projectId` or workspace path; the direct linkage is
329	runtime state (env var `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` / `ANTIGRAVITY_TRAJECTORY_ID`)
330	and/or inside encrypted `conversations/*.pb`. The CLI logs are therefore a
331	best-effort retained operational source, not transcript metadata.
332	
333	### 5.3 Recommended workspace-inference strategy for the parser
334	In priority order:
335	1. **history.jsonl `workspace`** keyed by matching `conversationId` — authoritative
336	   when present (interactive sessions only).
337	2. **CLI-log/config join** — map `conversationId -> projectId` from retained
338	   `antigravity-cli/log/cli-*.log`, then `projectId -> workspace` from
339	   `config/projects/*.json`.
340	3. **Tool-arg paths in the transcript** — derive the workspace from the most
341	   common ancestor of `Cwd` (run_command), `AbsolutePath` (view_file),
342	   `TargetFile` (write/edit), `SearchPath` (grep_search), `DirectoryPath`
343	   (list_dir). For print-mode `--add-dir` sessions these are absolute and
344	   consistently point at the workspace.
345	4. If none resolve (e.g. the no-`--add-dir` session that wandered the whole
346	   filesystem), mark workspace **unknown** — do not guess. Note: `agy -p` with no
347	   `--add-dir` defaults the workspace to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch`
348	   (an empty dir), so the model flails; such sessions have no meaningful project.
349	
350	---
351	
352	## 6. Annotated result-content examples (file tools)
353	
354	`VIEW_FILE` (result of `view_file`):
355	```
356	File Path: `file:///tmp/agy-recon-1779832704/main.go`
357	Total Lines: 9
358	Total Bytes: 98
359	Showing lines 1 to 9
360	The following code has been modified to include a line number before every line, in the format: <line_number>: <original_line>. ...
361	1: package main
362	2:
363	3: import "fmt"
364	...
365	The above content shows the entire, complete file contents of the requested file.
366	```
367	Strip the `N: ` line-number prefixes to recover original file content.
368	
369	`CODE_ACTION` (result of `write_to_file`):
370	```
371	Created file file:///tmp/agy-recon-1779832704/greeting.txt with requested content.
372	If relevant, proactively run terminal commands to execute this code for the USER. Don't ask for permission.
373	```
374	The actual written bytes are in the *call's* `CodeContent` arg, not the result.
375	
376	`CODE_ACTION` (result of `replace_file_content`):
377	```
378	The following changes were made by the replace_file_content tool to: /tmp/.../main.go. ...
379	[diff_block_start]
380	@@ -4,6 +4,6 @@
381	 ...
382	-	fmt.Println("hello world")
383	+	fmt.Println("goodbye world")
384	 ...
385	[diff_block_end]
386	```
387	Diff is between `[diff_block_start]`/`[diff_block_end]`; shows up to 3 context
388	lines. Old/new text are also in the call's `TargetContent`/`ReplacementContent`.
389	
390	`GREP_SEARCH` (result of `grep_search`):
391	```
392	{"File":"/tmp/agy-recon-1779832704/main.go","LineNumber":7,"LineContent":"\tfmt.Println(\"hello world\")"}
393	```
394	One JSON object per match line.
395	
396	`LIST_DIRECTORY` (result of `list_dir`):
397	```
398	{"name":".git", "isDir":true}
399	{"name":"README.md", "sizeBytes":"56"}
400	{"name":"main.go", "sizeBytes":"98"}
401	
402	Summary: This directory contains 1 subdirectories and 3 files.
403	```
404	
405	---
406	
407	## 7. Multi-turn / continuation behavior
408	
409	- `agy -c -p "..."` (continue most recent conversation) **appends to the SAME
410	  transcript file in the SAME `brain/<conversationId>/` dir.** No new brain dir,
411	  no new conversationId. Confirmed: the file grew from 11→14 lines.
412	- The continuation's `USER_INPUT` continues the monotonic `step_index` (e.g. a
413	  second turn's user input at index 12, right after the first turn ended at 11).
414	- A continuation turn's `USER_INPUT` content has `<USER_REQUEST>` +
415	  `<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>` but **no `<USER_SETTINGS_CHANGE>`** (settings unchanged).
416	- A turn boundary is marked at the start by either a `CONVERSATION_HISTORY`
417	  (`SYSTEM`) step or a `SYSTEM_MESSAGE` step. Detect new user turns by
418	  `type == "USER_INPUT"` occurrences rather than relying on a fixed structure.
419	- **Transcripts are append-only during and across turns** (writer appends one
420	  line per step; no rewriting of earlier lines was observed).
421	- `agy --conversation <id>` resumes a specific conversation by ID (per `--help`).
422	
423	---
424	
425	## 8. Version detection
426	
427	- **Command:** `agy --version`
428	- **Output:** a single line, just the semver, e.g.:
429	  ```
430	  1.0.2
431	  ```
432	  (no "v" prefix, no extra text; exit 0)
433	- Avoid `agy version` (no `--`): it tries to open a TTY and errors in
434	  non-interactive contexts (`bubbletea: could not open TTY`).
435	- `agy changelog` prints release notes grouped by version, newest first
436	  (`1.0.2:` then bullet lines prefixed with `·`, blank line, `1.0.1:` etc.) — also
437	  non-interactive and exit 0; the first `N.N.N:` line is the current version.
438	
439	---
440	
441	## 9. Auth note
442	`log/cli-*.log` repeatedly logs `Failed to poll ... You are not logged into
443	Antigravity.` yet sessions still receive model responses. Auth works off
444	`~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json` (keys: `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `id_token`,
445	`expiry_date`, `scope`, `token_type`). The log warnings are non-fatal; do not use
446	them as a "session failed" signal.
447	
448	---
449	
450	## 10. Edge cases (all verified unless noted)
451	
452	| case | behavior |
453	|---|---|
454	| Text-only session (no tools) | 3 steps: `USER_INPUT`(0), `CONVERSATION_HISTORY`(1), `PLANNER_RESPONSE`(2). No step_index gap. |
455	| Empty/aborted session | Not directly captured. A session that produces a `brain/` dir but a transcript with only steps 0–1 (no PLANNER_RESPONSE) would be an aborted/no-response session — treat absence of any `PLANNER_RESPONSE` as "no assistant output". |
456	| Failed shell command | `RUN_COMMAND` with `status:"DONE"` and content `"The command failed with exit code: N"`. NOT `ERROR`. |
457	| Tool-framework error | `status:"ERROR"`, content `"Encountered error in step execution: ..."` (e.g. dir not found). |
458	| Async / long command | `RUN_COMMAND` step with `status:"RUNNING"`; output later in `tasks/task-<N>.log`. |
459	| Parallel tool calls | Not observed (always 1 per PLANNER_RESPONSE) but tolerate `tool_calls` length >1. |
460	| Very large outputs | `list -la ~` was truncated in content with a literal `<truncated 494 lines>` marker. Expect inline truncation markers. |
461	| `.system_generated` naming | **Stable across runs** — every brain dir uses the literal `.system_generated/logs/` path; not randomized or regenerated under a different name. |
462	| `messages/` & `tasks/` dirs | Optional — only present when the session received a system message / ran an async task. Parser must tolerate their absence. |
463	| Append-only | Confirmed; transcripts are appended to, not rewritten. |
464	| Two transcript files | `transcript.jsonl` and `transcript_full.jsonl` always have identical line/step counts; only arg-escaping differs. |
465	
466	---
467	
468	## 11. Open questions / risks
469	
470	1. **conversationId → workspace has no canonical transcript metadata link** for
471	   print-mode sessions. history.jsonl covers interactive only. Retained CLI logs
472	   can join `conversationId -> projectId -> workspace`, but if logs rotate or are
473	   absent, workspace must be inferred from transcript tool-arg paths (§5.3).
474	   RISK: a text-only session with no history/log entry has no recoverable
475	   workspace.
476	2. **history.jsonl scope uncertainty.** Confirmed `-p` is excluded; unconfirmed
477	   whether `--prompt-interactive` (`-i`) writes to it. Assume only fully
478	   interactive TUI sessions are logged there.
479	3. **`implicit/*.pb` purpose unknown** (encrypted; different UUID namespace than
480	   conversationId, count happens to equal conversation count). Likely "implicit"
481	   memory/context blobs. Skip.
482	4. **Untested tools:** `codebase_search`, browser/URL tools (`read_url`,
483	   `execute_url`), MCP tools, subagent/task spawning. Their exact `args` keys and
484	   result `type` are unconfirmed — the only safe assumption is that an unknown
485	   tool's result is the next step and its `type` may be a new dedicated type or
486	   `GENERIC`. Parser should map by capability and default unknowns to generic.
487	5. **`thinking` field** carries model reasoning text. Map it to SpecStory's
488	   `thinking` content type, consistent with other providers; renderers can
489	   decide whether and how to expose it.
490	6. **The single index-4 gap** is inferred to be a hidden context-refresh step; its
491	   exact nature is not directly observable (it's never written to the transcript).
492	   Risk is low — treat the gap as benign, not data loss.
493	7. **`ANTIGRAVITY_SOURCE_METADATA` env var** (seen in an `env` command's captured
494	   output) contains a per-tool-call `id`, `thinkingSignature`, and the
495	   conversationId+stepIndex — this is the only place a call `id` surfaces, but
496	   it's incidental (only appears if the session happened to run `env`). Do not
497	   rely on it.
498

33	// SessionDataJSON marshals the session's normalized SessionData to a JSON string for

35	// stores and serves it verbatim), so it is pushed alongside the existing markdown and
36	// rawData. Returns "" (and logs) when there is no SessionData or marshaling fails, so
37	// callers can pass the result straight through — an empty payload simply means "no
38	// cloud-resumable blob for this session" and the server leaves session_data_size NULL.

40		if s == nil || s.SessionData == nil {

44		if err != nil {

33	// Check verifies that the Antigravity CLI is available and returns its resolved
34	// location and version (`agy --version` prints a bare semver such as "1.0.2").
35	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
36		cmdName, _ := parseCommand(customCommand)
37		isCustom := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != ""
38		slog.Info("Check: verifying Antigravity CLI installation",
39			"command", cmdName, "customCommand", isCustom)
40	
41		resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
42		if err != nil {
43			slog.Info("Check: binary not found on PATH", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
44			msg := buildCheckErrorMessage("not_found", cmdName, isCustom, "")
45			trackCheckFailure(providerID, isCustom, cmdName, "", versionFlag, "", "not_found", err.Error())
46			return spi.CheckResult{Success: false, Location: "", ErrorMessage: msg}
47		}
48		slog.Info("Check: binary resolved", "command", cmdName, "resolved", resolved)
49	
50		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
51		cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
52		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
53		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
54		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
55			errorType := classifyCheckError(err)
56			stderrOutput := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
57			slog.Info("Check: version probe failed",
58				"resolved", resolved, "errorType", errorType, "stderr", stderrOutput, "error", err)
59			msg := buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, resolved, isCustom, stderrOutput)
60			trackCheckFailure(providerID, isCustom, cmdName, resolved, versionFlag, stderrOutput, errorType, err.Error())
61			return spi.CheckResult{Success: false, Location: resolved, ErrorMessage: msg}
62		}
63	
64		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
65		if version == "" {
66			version = "unknown"
67		}
68		slog.Info("Check: succeeded", "resolved", resolved, "version", version)
69		trackCheckSuccess(providerID, isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version, versionFlag)
70		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
71	}

76		files, err := listConversationFiles()

80			}
81			return false

87			return false
88		}

90			return true
91		}
92	
93		history, _ := loadHistoryIndex()
94		projectWorkspaces, _ := loadConversationWorkspaceIndex()
95		for _, file := range files {

97			if err != nil {

99			}
100			if sessionMatchesProject(session, projectPath) {

102			}
103		}
104	
105		if helpOutput {

109	}

117		}
118		history, _ := loadHistoryIndex()
119		projectWorkspaces, _ := loadConversationWorkspaceIndex()
120	
121		total := len(files)
122		result := make([]spi.AgentChatSession, 0, total)
123		for i, file := range files {
124			session, err := parseTranscript(file.ConversationID, file.Path, history, projectWorkspaces, true)
125			if err != nil {
126				slog.Debug("antigravity: skipping session", "conversationId", file.ConversationID, "error", err)
127				if progress != nil {
128					progress(i+1, total)
129				}
130				continue
131			}
132			if !sessionMatchesProject(session, projectPath) {
133				if progress != nil {
134					progress(i+1, total)
135				}
136				continue
137			}
138			if chat := convertToAgentSession(session, projectPath, debugRaw); chat != nil {
139				result = append(result, *chat)
140			}
141			if progress != nil {
142				progress(i+1, total)
143			}
144		}
145		return result, nil
146	}
147	
148	// GetAgentChatSession returns the session with the given conversation ID.
149	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath string, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
150		path, err := findTranscriptByID(sessionID)
151		if err != nil || path == "" {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		history, _ := loadHistoryIndex()
155		projectWorkspaces, _ := loadConversationWorkspaceIndex()
156		session, err := parseTranscript(sessionID, path, history, projectWorkspaces, true)
157		if err != nil {
158			return nil, err
159		}
160		// When a session is explicitly requested by id, exclude it only if it has a
161		// known workspace that mismatches the project. Unscoped sessions (text-only
162		// print-mode, no recoverable workspace) are returned as requested.
163		if strings.TrimSpace(projectPath) != "" && sessionWorkspaceKnown(session) && !sessionMatchesProject(session, projectPath) {
164			return nil, nil
165		}
166		return convertToAgentSession(session, projectPath, debugRaw), nil
167	}
168	
169	// ListAgentChatSessions returns lightweight metadata for all sessions without
170	// retaining full session content.
171	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
172		files, err := listConversationFiles()
173		if err != nil {
174			return nil, err
175		}
176		history, _ := loadHistoryIndex()
177		projectWorkspaces, _ := loadConversationWorkspaceIndex()
178	
179		var result []spi.SessionMetadata
180		for _, file := range files {
181			session, err := parseTranscript(file.ConversationID, file.Path, history, projectWorkspaces, false)
182			if err != nil {
183				slog.Debug("antigravity: failed to parse session", "conversationId", file.ConversationID, "error", err)
184				continue
185			}
186			if !sessionMatchesProject(session, projectPath) {
187				continue
188			}
189			meta := sessionMetadata(session, history)
190			if meta == nil {
191				slog.Debug("antigravity: skipping session with no user prompt", "conversationId", file.ConversationID)
192				continue
193			}
194			result = append(result, *meta)
195		}
196	
197		return result, nil
198	}
199	
200	// ExecAgentAndWatch executes the Antigravity CLI for the given project and
201	// watches for transcript updates.
202	func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
203		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: starting Antigravity CLI execution and monitoring",
204			"projectPath", projectPath,
205			"customCommand", customCommand,
206			"resumeSessionID", resumeSessionID,
207			"debugRaw", debugRaw,
208			"hasCallback", sessionCallback != nil)
209	
210		if sessionCallback == nil {
211			slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: no callback provided, running without watcher")
212			return ExecuteAntigravity(customCommand, resumeSessionID)
213		}
214	
215		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
216		defer cancel()
217	
218		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: launching session watcher in background")
219		watchErr := make(chan error, 1)
220		go func() {
221			watchErr <- watchSessions(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
222		}()
223	
224		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: executing Antigravity CLI", "command", customCommand)
225		err := ExecuteAntigravity(customCommand, resumeSessionID)
226		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: Antigravity CLI exited, stopping watcher", "execError", err)
227		cancel()
228	
229		if werr := <-watchErr; werr != nil && !errors.Is(werr, context.Canceled) {
230			slog.Warn("ExecAgentAndWatch: watcher stopped with error", "error", werr)
231		}
232	
233		if err != nil {
234			return fmt.Errorf("antigravity execution failed: %w", err)
235		}
236		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: complete")
237		return nil
238	}
239	
240	// WatchAgent monitors Antigravity CLI sessions for the given project and invokes
241	// sessionCallback for each new or updated session until ctx is canceled.
242	func (p *Provider) WatchAgent(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
243		slog.Info("WatchAgent: starting Antigravity CLI activity monitoring",
244			"projectPath", projectPath, "debugRaw", debugRaw)
245		if sessionCallback == nil {
246			return fmt.Errorf("session callback is required")
247		}
248		err := watchSessions(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
249		slog.Info("WatchAgent: watcher exited", "error", err)
250		return err
251	}
252	
253	// --- helpers shared across the package ---
254	
255	func classifyCheckError(err error) string {
256		var execErr *exec.Error
257		var pathErr *os.PathError
258		switch {
259		case errors.As(err, &execErr) && execErr.Err == exec.ErrNotFound:
260			return "not_found"
261		case errors.As(err, &pathErr) && errors.Is(pathErr.Err, os.ErrPermission):
262			return "permission_denied"
263		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
264			return "permission_denied"
265		default:
266			return "version_failed"
267		}
268	}
269	
270	func buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType string, command string, isCustom bool, stderr string) string {
271		var builder strings.Builder
272		switch errorType {
273		case "not_found":
274			builder.WriteString("Antigravity CLI was not found.\n\n")
275			if isCustom {
276				builder.WriteString("• Verify the custom path you provided is executable.\n")
277				fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "• Provided command: %s\n", command)
278			} else {
279				builder.WriteString("• Install the Antigravity CLI and ensure `agy` is on your PATH.\n")
280				builder.WriteString("• Re-run `specstory check antigravity` after installation.\n")
281			}
282		case "permission_denied":
283			builder.WriteString("SpecStory cannot execute the Antigravity CLI due to permissions.\n\n")
284			fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "Try: chmod +x %s\n", command)
285		default:
286			builder.WriteString("`agy --version` failed.\n\n")
287			if stderr != "" {
288				builder.WriteString("Error output:\n")
289				builder.WriteString(stderr)
290				builder.WriteString("\n\n")
291			}
292			builder.WriteString("Run `agy --version` manually to diagnose, then retry.")
293		}
294		return builder.String()
295	}

13	// GlobalSessionRef is a lightweight, project-discovering reference to a single
14	// native session, returned by Provider.ListAllAgentChatSessions.
15	//
16	// Unlike the project-scoped ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath), the project is NOT
17	// an input here: each ref carries the originating working directory (read from inside
18	// the session) so the caller — the `specstory reindex` command — can resolve project
19	// identity with utils.ComputeProjectID. The project is discovered, not supplied.
20	//
21	// It is intentionally metadata-only (no full SessionData parse); reindex re-fetches
22	// full data per ref via GetAgentChatSession(OriginCwd, SessionID) when it needs the
23	// conversation body. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
24	type GlobalSessionRef struct {
25		SessionID  string // native session id (uuid)
26		CreatedAt  string // ISO 8601 creation timestamp (first turn), may be empty
27		Slug       string // filename-safe slug derived from the first user message
28		Name       string // human-readable description (may be empty)
29		NativePath string // absolute path the provider opens to read this session
30		OriginCwd  string // working directory the session was launched from (-> project_id)
31	}
32	
33	// PathSessionReader is an OPTIONAL capability a Provider may implement: parse a single
34	// session directly from its already-known native file path, skipping the by-id discovery
35	// search that GetAgentChatSession performs.
36	//
37	// Why: some providers locate a session by scanning their native store. Codex's by-id
38	// lookup walks the entire ~/.codex/sessions tree on every call, so resolving N sessions
39	// that way is O(N²). reindex already holds each session's exact file path
40	// (GlobalSessionRef.NativePath) from enumeration, so a path-keyed parse turns that back
41	// into O(N). reindex prefers this when a provider implements it and the ref carries a
42	// NativePath, and falls back to GetAgentChatSession otherwise.
43	//
44	// originCwd is the session's originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd),
45	// passed through as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
46	// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath.
47	type PathSessionReader interface {
48		GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath string, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*AgentChatSession, error)
49	}
50	
51	// ScanReporter accumulates a provider's enumeration progress (sessions found) so the CLI can
52	// render a live "scanning" display. It is safe for concurrent use and safe to call on a nil
53	// receiver (a no-op), so providers can report unconditionally.
54	type ScanReporter struct {
55		found atomic.Int64
56	}
57	
58	// Add records that n more sessions have been found. Files that yield no session (warmup-only or
59	// sidechain-only transcripts) are deliberately not counted, so the running total reflects real
60	// sessions rather than raw files.
61	func (r *ScanReporter) Add(n int) {
62		if r != nil {
63			r.found.Add(int64(n))
64		}
65	}
66	
67	// Found returns the number of sessions found so far.
68	func (r *ScanReporter) Found() int64 {
69		if r == nil {
70			return 0
71		}
72		return r.found.Load()
73	}
74	
75	// ProgressEnumerator is an OPTIONAL Provider capability: enumerate all sessions while reporting
76	// scan progress into r (which may be nil — ScanReporter is nil-safe, so report unconditionally).
77	// Providers that don't implement it are enumerated via ListAllAgentChatSessions with no live
78	// feedback. reindex uses this to render a per-agent "Scanning agents…" display.
79	type ProgressEnumerator interface {
80		ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *ScanReporter) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error)
81	}
82	
83	// ScanSessionsInParallel walks root for *.jsonl session files and scans each one concurrently
84	// with scan, returning the collected refs. It is the shared engine behind each provider's
85	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress: providers differ only in where their sessions live (root)
86	// and how a single file's header maps to a GlobalSessionRef (scan).
87	//
88	// scan returns (ref, nil) to include a session, (nil, nil) to skip a non-session file
89	// (warmup-only / empty / sidechain-only), or (nil, err) to log-and-skip a malformed file.
90	// Files are independent and the per-file read+parse is CPU-bound, so scanning fans out across
91	// CPUs; output order is unspecified (reindex dedups and sorts later). r counts sessions found
92	// (not files scanned) and is nil-safe. label names the provider in scan-failure logs.
93	func ScanSessionsInParallel(root, label string, r *ScanReporter, scan func(path string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error)) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error) {
94		// Phase 1: collect file paths (dirents only — no opens).
95		var paths []string
96		walkErr := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
97			if err != nil {
98				return nil // skip unreadable entries rather than abort the whole sweep
99			}
100			if d.IsDir() || filepath.Ext(path) != ".jsonl" {
101				return nil
102			}
103			paths = append(paths, path)
104			return nil
105		})
106		if walkErr != nil {
107			return nil, fmt.Errorf("walking %s sessions: %w", label, walkErr)
108		}
109	
110		// Phase 2: scan headers in parallel. min(NumCPU, 12) is always ≥ 1, so no lower-bound guard.
111		workers := min(runtime.NumCPU(), 12)
112		pathCh := make(chan string, workers)
113		refs := make([]GlobalSessionRef, 0, len(paths))
114		var mu sync.Mutex
115		var wg sync.WaitGroup
116		for i := 0; i < workers; i++ {
117			wg.Add(1)
118			go func() {
119				defer wg.Done()
120				for path := range pathCh {
121					ref, scanErr := safeScan(scan, path)
122					if scanErr != nil {
123						slog.Warn("reindex: failed to scan session", "agent", label, "path", path, "error", scanErr)
124						continue
125					}
126					if ref == nil {
127						continue // not a session (warmup / empty / sidechain)
128					}
129					mu.Lock()
130					refs = append(refs, *ref)
131					mu.Unlock()
132					r.Add(1) // count sessions found, not files scanned
133				}
134			}()
135		}
136		for _, path := range paths {
137			pathCh <- path
138		}
139		close(pathCh)
140		wg.Wait()
141		return refs, nil
142	}
143	
144	// safeScan runs scan(path), converting a panic into an error so one malformed session file is
145	// logged and skipped (via the caller's normal error path) rather than crashing the whole sweep.
146	func safeScan(scan func(string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error), path string) (ref *GlobalSessionRef, err error) {
147		defer func() {
148			if r := recover(); r != nil {
149				ref, err = nil, fmt.Errorf("panic scanning session: %v", r)
150			}
151		}()
152		return scan(path)
153	}
