11	// ErrReconstructionUnsupported is returned by a provider that carries the
12	// ReconstructSession responsibility but does not yet have a native serializer.
13	// Reconstruction is on the Provider interface so every provider implements the
14	// method, but only some providers (initially Claude Code and Codex CLI) produce
15	// real native output.
16	var ErrReconstructionUnsupported = errors.New("session reconstruction not supported by this provider")
17	
18	// ReconstructOptions controls how a session is reconstructed into native form.
19	type ReconstructOptions struct {
20		// WorkspaceRoot is the target working directory the reconstructed session
21		// should belong to. Native paths/IDs are derived from it. When empty, the
22		// provider falls back to the SessionData's own WorkspaceRoot.
23		WorkspaceRoot string
24	
25		// MigrationNote, when set, is prepended as a leading agent turn so the agent
26		// understands the prior turns were imported from another session. Optional.
27		MigrationNote string
28	}
29	
30	// ReconstructedSession is the native output of reconstruction. It is data only;
31	// the caller decides where (and whether) to write it.
32	type ReconstructedSession struct {
33		SessionID string // freshly minted, native-format session ID
34		Filename  string // suggested native filename (base name, not a full path)
35		Content   []byte // native session file bytes
36	}
37	
38	// Turn is a single role-tagged text turn in the flattened transcript. The
39	// reconstruction model collapses everything an agent said, thought, or did into
40	// plain user/agent text turns (see docs/SESSION-PORTABILITY.md), which each
41	// provider then serializes into its native format.
42	type Turn struct {
43		Role string // schema.RoleUser or schema.RoleAgent
44		Text string
45	}
46	
47	// FlattenSessionData reduces a SessionData into an ordered list of plain
48	// user/agent text turns. This is the single place the cross-provider flattening
49	// policy lives, so every provider's serializer consumes the same transcript.
50	//
51	// Rules (per the locked design):
52	//   - user/agent text content -> a turn of that role
53	//   - thinking content -> folded into the agent turn's text (not dropped)
54	//   - tool calls -> folded into the agent turn's text via the pre-rendered
55	//     Summary / FormattedMarkdown captured on the forward pass
56	//   - model, usage, and path hints -> dropped
57	//
58	// migrationNote, when non-empty, becomes a leading agent turn.
59	func FlattenSessionData(data *schema.SessionData, migrationNote string) []Turn {
60		var turns []Turn
61	
62		if strings.TrimSpace(migrationNote) != "" {
63			turns = append(turns, Turn{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Text: strings.TrimSpace(migrationNote)})
64		}
65	
66		if data == nil {
67			return turns
68		}
69	
70		for i := range data.Exchanges {
71			for j := range data.Exchanges[i].Messages {
72				msg := &data.Exchanges[i].Messages[j]
73	
74				// Only user and agent roles produce turns; anything else is skipped.
75				if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser && msg.Role != schema.RoleAgent {
76					continue
77				}
78	
79				text := messageTurnText(msg)
80				if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" {
81					continue
82				}
83	
84				// Drop synthetic, non-conversational turns (slash-command invocations,
85				// local-command output, etc.) so they are not replayed into the resumed
86				// session. This is intentionally reconstruction-only — archival markdown
87				// stays faithful to the source session.
88				if isSyntheticTurnText(text) {
89					continue
90				}
91	
92				turns = append(turns, Turn{Role: msg.Role, Text: text})
93			}
94		}
95	
96		return turns
97	}
98	
99	// PrepareTurns validates session data and flattens it into the neutral turn list
100	// every provider's serializer consumes. It centralizes the two guards each
101	// ReconstructSession must apply before it can build native output: the source
102	// SessionData must be non-nil, and flattening must yield at least one turn.
103	// Keeping these here means every provider rejects the same cases with the same
104	// messages and cannot drift apart.
105	func PrepareTurns(data *schema.SessionData, opts ReconstructOptions) ([]Turn, error) {
106		if data == nil {
107			return nil, errors.New("cannot reconstruct nil session data")
108		}
109	
110		turns := FlattenSessionData(data, opts.MigrationNote)
111		if len(turns) == 0 {
112			return nil, errors.New("session has no content to reconstruct")
113		}
114	
115		return turns, nil
116	}
117	
118	// ResolveWorkspaceRoot picks the working directory a reconstructed session
119	// belongs to: the explicit target from opts when set, otherwise the source
120	// session's own recorded root. Providers derive native paths/IDs from the
121	// result; the cursor provider is the lone exception that needs no workspace.
122	func ResolveWorkspaceRoot(opts ReconstructOptions, data *schema.SessionData) string {
123		if opts.WorkspaceRoot != "" {
124			return opts.WorkspaceRoot
125		}
126		if data == nil {
127			return ""
128		}
129		return data.WorkspaceRoot
130	}
131	
132	// reconstructMillisLayout is the RFC 3339 millisecond layout with a literal Z that the
133	// Claude Code, Codex, Droid, and Gemini serializers stamp on reconstructed records.
134	// (DeepSeek uses microsecond precision and formats its own.)
135	const reconstructMillisLayout = "2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z"
136	
137	// RFC3339Millis formats t with millisecond precision and a literal Z, the timestamp shape
138	// shared by the Claude/Codex/Droid/Gemini serializers. Callers pass a UTC time.
139	func RFC3339Millis(t time.Time) string {
140		return t.Format(reconstructMillisLayout)
141	}
142	
143	// ResumedSessionTitle returns the display title for a reconstructed session: the trimmed
144	// source slug, or "Resumed session" when the slug is blank or whitespace-only. Centralizing
145	// this keeps the trim (which a couple of serializers previously skipped) and the fallback
146	// consistent across providers.
147	func ResumedSessionTitle(slug string) string {
148		if title := strings.TrimSpace(slug); title != "" {
149			return title
150		}
151		return "Resumed session"
152	}
153	
154	// ReconstructRole maps a flattened Turn role to the "user"/"assistant" role string used by
155	// most native session formats. Providers with a different role vocabulary (e.g. Gemini's
156	// "gemini", Codex's event labels) map their own.
157	func ReconstructRole(role string) string {
158		if role == schema.RoleUser {
159			return "user"
160		}
161		return "assistant"
162	}
163	
164	// SyntheticCommandTags are the wrapper tags coding agents inject for
165	// non-conversational slash-command records: the command invocation, its piped
166	// local stdout/stderr, and the local-command caveat. They are conversation
167	// scaffolding, never a real user prompt. This is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for
168	// the tag set, shared by reconstruction's turn filter here (matched anywhere in a
169	// flattened turn) and Claude Code's title-selection filter
170	// (claudecode.isSyntheticMessage, matched as a leading tag), so the two cannot
171	// drift apart.
172	var SyntheticCommandTags = []string{
173		"<command-name>",
174		"<command-message>",
175		"<command-args>",
176		"<local-command-stdout>",
177		"<local-command-stderr>",
178		"<local-command-caveat>",
179	}
180	
181	// extraSyntheticTurnMarkers are synthetic markers beyond the shared command tags
182	// that must also never be replayed into a resumed session: Claude Code's
183	// <TEXTBLOCK> title-generation wrapper and its interrupt marker (which also has a
184	// "…for tool use" variant, caught by the prefix).
185	var extraSyntheticTurnMarkers = []string{
186		"<TEXTBLOCK>",
187		"[Request interrupted by user",
188	}
189	
190	// isSyntheticTurnText reports whether a flattened turn is a synthetic,
191	// non-conversational artifact that should not be replayed into a resumed session.
192	// It matches by Contains because a flattened turn concatenates content parts, so a
193	// marker can appear anywhere in the text. Markdown generation does NOT use this
194	// filter and stays faithful to source.
195	func isSyntheticTurnText(text string) bool {
196		for _, marker := range SyntheticCommandTags {
197			if strings.Contains(text, marker) {
198				return true
199			}
200		}
201		for _, marker := range extraSyntheticTurnMarkers {
202			if strings.Contains(text, marker) {
203				return true
204			}
205		}
206		return false
207	}
208	
209	// messageTurnText flattens a single message into its turn text: all text/thinking
210	// content parts joined, followed by the tool's pre-rendered markdown when present.
211	func messageTurnText(msg *schema.Message) string {
212		var parts []string
213	
214		for _, part := range msg.Content {
215			// Both "text" and "thinking" parts carry their content in Text; thinking
216			// is intentionally treated as ordinary agent text.
217			if strings.TrimSpace(part.Text) != "" {
218				parts = append(parts, part.Text)
219			}
220		}
221	
222		text := strings.Join(parts, "\n\n")
223	
224		if msg.Tool != nil {
225			toolText := toolTurnText(msg.Tool)
226			if toolText != "" {
227				if text != "" {
228					text += "\n\n" + toolText
229				} else {
230					text = toolText
231				}
232			}
233		}
234	
235		return text
236	}
237	
238	// toolTurnText renders a tool call as agent text, reusing the markdown the
239	// forward pass already produced (Summary + FormattedMarkdown). Falls back to a
240	// minimal description when neither is available.
241	func toolTurnText(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
242		var b strings.Builder
243	
244		if tool.Summary != nil && strings.TrimSpace(*tool.Summary) != "" {
245			b.WriteString(strings.TrimSpace(*tool.Summary))
246		}
247	
248		if tool.FormattedMarkdown != nil && strings.TrimSpace(*tool.FormattedMarkdown) != "" {
249			if b.Len() > 0 {
250				b.WriteString("\n\n")
251			}
252			b.WriteString(strings.TrimRight(*tool.FormattedMarkdown, "\n"))
253		}
254	
255		if b.Len() == 0 {
256			// Nothing pre-rendered; emit a minimal, non-empty description so the tool
257			// activity is at least acknowledged in the transcript.
258			b.WriteString("Tool use: " + tool.Name)
259		}
260	
261		return b.String()
262	}
263

55	// convertToAgentSession converts a parsed agSession into the unified

57	func convertToAgentSession(session *agSession, workspaceRoot string, debugRaw bool) *spi.AgentChatSession {

60		}

76			Slug:        sessionData.Slug,
77			SessionData: sessionData,

82	// generateAgentSession converts an agSession into the shared SessionData schema.
83	func generateAgentSession(session *agSession, workspaceRoot string) (*SessionData, error) {
84		// Prefer the session's own resolved workspace; fall back to the project the
85		// CLI is syncing from so WorkspaceRoot is never empty.
86		workspace := strings.TrimSpace(workspaceRoot)
87		if ws := strings.TrimSpace(session.Workspace); ws != "" {
88			workspace = ws
89		}
90	
91		exchanges := buildExchanges(session, workspace)
92		if len(exchanges) == 0 {
93			return nil, fmt.Errorf("session contains no conversational exchanges")
94		}
95	
96		created := strings.TrimSpace(session.CreatedAt)
97		updated := strings.TrimSpace(session.UpdatedAt)
98		if updated == "" {
99			updated = created
100		}
101	
102		// Provider.Version must be non-empty for schema validation. Antigravity does
103		// not stamp the model on every step, so we use the model derived from the
104		// first turn's settings block and fall back to "unknown".
105		version := strings.TrimSpace(session.Model)
106		if version == "" {
107			version = "unknown"
108		}
109	
110		// Antigravity surfaces no per-step token usage in the transcript, so — like
111		// DeepSeek TUI — we intentionally do not synthesize a schema.Usage value.
112	
113		data := &SessionData{
114			SchemaVersion: "1.0",
115			Provider: ProviderInfo{
116				ID:      providerSchemaID,
117				Name:    providerName,
118				Version: version,
119			},
120			SessionID:     session.ConversationID,
121			CreatedAt:     created,
122			UpdatedAt:     updated,
123			Slug:          deriveSlug(session),
124			WorkspaceRoot: workspace,
125			Exchanges:     exchanges,
126		}
127	
128		return data, nil
129	}

131	// buildExchanges groups transcript steps into exchanges. Steps are processed in
132	// file order (NOT by step_index — the index has a benign gap at 4). Each
133	// USER_INPUT starts a new exchange; PLANNER_RESPONSE adds an agent text message
134	// plus one message per tool call; a tool-result step attaches its output to the
135	// matching pending tool message.
136	func buildExchanges(session *agSession, workspaceRoot string) []Exchange {
137		var exchanges []Exchange
138		var current *Exchange
139	
140		flush := func() {
141			if current != nil && len(current.Messages) > 0 {
142				exchanges = append(exchanges, *current)
143			}
144		}
145	
146		for _, step := range session.Steps {
147			switch {
148			case step.Type == typeUserInput && step.Source == sourceUserExplicit:
149				flush()
150				current = &Exchange{}
151				msg := convertUserStep(step)
152				if len(msg.Content) > 0 {
153					current.Messages = append(current.Messages, msg)
154					current.StartTime = step.CreatedAt
155					current.EndTime = step.CreatedAt
156				}
157	
158			case step.Type == typePlannerResponse:
159				if current == nil {
160					current = &Exchange{}
161				}
162				current.Messages = append(current.Messages, convertPlannerStep(step, session.ConversationID, session.Model, workspaceRoot)...)
163				current.EndTime = step.CreatedAt
164	
165			case isToolResultType(step.Type):
166				// Tool results carry source MODEL and immediately follow their
167				// PLANNER_RESPONSE; they are not new turns.
168				if current != nil {
169					attachToolResult(step, current, session.TaskOutputs)
170					current.EndTime = step.CreatedAt
171				}
172	
173			case step.Type == typeConversationHistory, step.Type == typeSystemMessage:
174				// Replayed context / injected notices — not user-visible turn content.
175				continue
176	
177			default:
178				slog.Debug("antigravity: skipping unrecognized step",
179					"conversationId", session.ConversationID, "type", step.Type, "stepIndex", step.StepIndex)
180			}
181		}
182	
183		flush()
184	
185		for i := range exchanges {
186			exchanges[i].ExchangeID = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", session.ConversationID, i)
187			if exchanges[i].StartTime == "" {
188				exchanges[i].StartTime = session.CreatedAt
189			}
190			if exchanges[i].EndTime == "" {
191				exchanges[i].EndTime = exchanges[i].StartTime
192			}
193		}
194	
195		return exchanges
196	}
197	
198	// convertUserStep converts a USER_INPUT step to a schema user message, stripping
199	// the <USER_REQUEST> wrapper and metadata blocks. Returns a zero-value Message
200	// (empty Content) when nothing user-visible remains; callers drop it.
201	func convertUserStep(step transcriptStep) Message {
202		text := cleanUserPrompt(step.Content)
203		if text == "" {
204			return Message{}
205		}
206		return Message{
207			Timestamp: step.CreatedAt,
208			Role:      schema.RoleUser,
209			Content:   []ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: text}},
210		}
211	}
212	
213	// convertPlannerStep converts a PLANNER_RESPONSE into an ordered set of messages:
214	// an optional agent message carrying the model's thinking + reply text, followed
215	// by one message per tool call.
216	func convertPlannerStep(step transcriptStep, conversationID, model, workspaceRoot string) []Message {
217		var msgs []Message
218	
219		var parts []ContentPart
220		if thinking := strings.TrimSpace(step.Thinking); thinking != "" {
221			parts = append(parts, ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeThinking, Text: thinking})
222		}
223		if text := strings.TrimSpace(step.Content); text != "" {
224			parts = append(parts, ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: text})
225		}
226		if len(parts) > 0 {
227			msgs = append(msgs, Message{
228				Timestamp: step.CreatedAt,
229				Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
230				Model:     model,
231				Content:   parts,
232			})
233		}
234	
235		for idx, tc := range step.ToolCalls {
236			// Antigravity tool calls carry no explicit id, so synthesize a stable one
237			// from the conversation + step + tool position.
238			useID := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d:%d", conversationID, step.StepIndex, idx)
239			msgs = append(msgs, convertToolCallMessage(tc, useID, model, step.CreatedAt, workspaceRoot))
240		}
241	
242		return msgs
243	}
244	
245	// convertToolCallMessage builds an agent Message for a single tool call. The
246	// FormattedMarkdown is set from the input here; attachToolResult re-renders it
247	// once the matching result step lands.
248	func convertToolCallMessage(tc transcriptToolCall, useID, model, timestamp, workspaceRoot string) Message {
249		name := tc.Name
250		if name == "" {
251			name = "unknown"
252		}
253		tool := &ToolInfo{
254			Name:  name,
255			Type:  classifyToolType(name),
256			UseID: useID,
257			Input: tc.Args,
258		}
259		if formatted := formatToolCall(tool); formatted != "" {
260			tool.FormattedMarkdown = &formatted
261		}
262		return Message{
263			Timestamp: timestamp,
264			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
265			Model:     model,
266			Tool:      tool,
267			PathHints: extractPathHints(tc.Args, workspaceRoot),
268		}
269	}
270	
271	// attachToolResult routes a tool-result step's content to the oldest tool
272	// message in the current exchange that has not yet received output (FIFO).
273	// Correlation is positional because Antigravity transcripts carry no call→result
274	// id. After attaching, the tool's FormattedMarkdown is re-rendered to include
275	// the output.
276	func attachToolResult(step transcriptStep, current *Exchange, taskOutputs map[int]string) {
277		content := cleanResultContent(step)
278		if strings.EqualFold(step.Status, "RUNNING") {
279			if taskOutput := strings.TrimSpace(taskOutputs[step.StepIndex]); taskOutput != "" {
280				if content != "" {
281					content += "\n\nTask output:\n" + taskOutput
282				} else {
283					content = taskOutput
284				}
285			}
286		}
287		for i := range current.Messages {
288			tool := current.Messages[i].Tool
289			if tool == nil || tool.Output != nil {
290				continue
291			}
292			tool.Output = map[string]any{"content": content}
293			if formatted := formatToolCall(tool); formatted != "" {
294				tool.FormattedMarkdown = &formatted
295			}
296			return
297		}
298		slog.Debug("antigravity: tool result with no pending tool call", "type", step.Type, "stepIndex", step.StepIndex)
299	}
300	
301	// cleanResultContent returns a tool result's content with the leading tab
302	// indentation that Antigravity inserts into RUN_COMMAND output blocks removed.
303	func cleanResultContent(step transcriptStep) string {
304		content := strings.TrimSpace(step.Content)
305		if content == "" {
306			return ""
307		}
308		lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
309		for i, line := range lines {
310			lines[i] = strings.TrimLeft(line, "\t")
311		}
312		return strings.TrimSpace(strings.Join(lines, "\n"))
313	}
314	
315	// cleanUserPrompt extracts the real prompt from a USER_INPUT content blob.
316	func cleanUserPrompt(raw string) string {
317		if m := userRequestRe.FindStringSubmatch(raw); len(m) == 2 {
318			return strings.TrimSpace(m[1])
319		}
320		// No wrapper (defensive): drop any metadata blocks and return the remainder.
321		cleaned := metadataBlockRe.ReplaceAllString(raw, "")
322		return strings.TrimSpace(cleaned)
323	}
324	
325	// deriveSlug builds a filename-safe slug from the first user prompt.
326	func deriveSlug(session *agSession) string {
327		if prompt := firstUserPromptText(session); prompt != "" {
328			if slug := spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(prompt); slug != "" {
329				return slug
330			}
331		}
332		return fallbackSlug
333	}
334	
335	// deriveModel extracts the model name from the first turn's settings-change
336	// block. Returns "" when no model is recorded (e.g. continuation-only captures).
337	func deriveModel(steps []transcriptStep) string {
338		for _, step := range steps {
339			if step.Type != typeUserInput {
340				continue
341			}
342			if m := modelRe.FindStringSubmatch(step.Content); len(m) == 2 {
343				return strings.TrimSpace(m[1])
344			}
345		}
346		return ""
347	}
348	
349	// resolveSessionWorkspace determines the workspace a conversation belongs to.
350	// history.jsonl is authoritative when it has an entry (interactive sessions).
351	// Otherwise, retained CLI logs can join conversationId -> projectId -> workspace.
352	// Finally, the workspace is inferred as the common ancestor of absolute paths
353	// touched by tools. Returns "" when nothing is resolvable.
354	func resolveSessionWorkspace(conversationID string, steps []transcriptStep, history map[string]historyEntry, projectWorkspaces map[string]string) string {
355		if entry, ok := history[conversationID]; ok {
356			if ws := strings.TrimSpace(entry.Workspace); ws != "" {
357				return ws
358			}
359		}
360		if ws := strings.TrimSpace(projectWorkspaces[conversationID]); ws != "" {
361			return ws
362		}
363		return commonPathPrefix(collectWorkspacePaths(steps))
364	}
365	
366	// sessionWorkspaceKnown reports whether a session has any signal of which
367	// project it belongs to. Text-only print-mode sessions have neither a history
368	// entry nor tool paths, so their workspace is unknowable; such "unscoped"
369	// sessions are surfaced only on explicit by-id retrieval, never in project-
370	// filtered bulk listings (which would otherwise pollute every project).
371	func sessionWorkspaceKnown(session *agSession) bool {
372		return strings.TrimSpace(session.Workspace) != "" || len(collectToolPaths(session.Steps)) > 0
373	}
374	
375	// sessionMatchesProject reports whether a session belongs to projectPath. An
376	// empty projectPath matches every session (no filtering). A session matches when
377	// its resolved workspace and the project are nested either way, or when any tool
378	// touched a path inside the project.
379	func sessionMatchesProject(session *agSession, projectPath string) bool {
380		if strings.TrimSpace(projectPath) == "" {
381			return true
382		}
383		if session.Workspace != "" {
384			if pathWithin(session.Workspace, projectPath) || pathWithin(projectPath, session.Workspace) {
385				return true
386			}
387		}
388		for _, p := range collectToolPaths(session.Steps) {
389			if pathWithin(p, projectPath) {
390				return true
391			}
392		}
393		return false
394	}
395	
396	// collectToolPaths gathers the absolute filesystem paths referenced by every
397	// tool call in the transcript, normalizing file:// URIs to plain paths.
398	func collectToolPaths(steps []transcriptStep) []string {
399		var paths []string
400		seen := make(map[string]bool)
401		for _, step := range steps {
402			for _, tc := range step.ToolCalls {
403				for _, key := range toolPathArgKeys {
404					val, ok := tc.Args[key].(string)
405					if !ok {
406						continue
407					}
408					appendUniqueAbsPath(&paths, seen, val)
409				}
410			}
411		}
412		return paths
413	}
414	
415	// collectWorkspacePaths gathers directory candidates for workspace inference.
416	// File-valued tool args are reduced to their parent directory; directory-valued
417	// args are used as-is.
418	func collectWorkspacePaths(steps []transcriptStep) []string {
419		var paths []string
420		seen := make(map[string]bool)
421		add := func(value string, fileValue bool) {
422			p := stripFileURI(strings.TrimSpace(value))
423			if p == "" || !filepath.IsAbs(p) {
424				return
425			}
426			if fileValue {
427				p = filepath.Dir(p)
428			}
429			appendUniqueAbsPath(&paths, seen, p)
430		}
431	
432		for _, step := range steps {
433			for _, tc := range step.ToolCalls {
434				for _, key := range workspaceDirArgKeys {
435					if val, ok := tc.Args[key].(string); ok {
436						add(val, false)
437					}
438				}
439				for _, key := range workspaceFileArgKeys {
440					if val, ok := tc.Args[key].(string); ok {
441						add(val, true)
442					}
443				}
444			}
445		}
446		return paths
447	}
448	
449	func appendUniqueAbsPath(paths *[]string, seen map[string]bool, value string) {
450		p := stripFileURI(strings.TrimSpace(value))
451		if p == "" || !filepath.IsAbs(p) || seen[p] {
452			return
453		}
454		seen[p] = true
455		*paths = append(*paths, p)
456	}
457	
458	// commonPathPrefix returns the deepest directory that is an ancestor of every
459	// given absolute path, or "" when the slice is empty or paths share no common
460	// root.
461	func commonPathPrefix(paths []string) string {
462		if len(paths) == 0 {
463			return ""
464		}
465	
466		split := func(p string) []string {
467			return strings.Split(filepath.Clean(p), string(filepath.Separator))
468		}
469	
470		common := split(paths[0])
471		for _, p := range paths[1:] {
472			parts := split(p)
473			n := len(common)
474			if len(parts) < n {
475				n = len(parts)
476			}
477			i := 0
478			for i < n && common[i] == parts[i] {
479				i++
480			}
481			common = common[:i]
482		}
483	
484		if len(common) <= 1 {
485			return ""
486		}
487		return strings.Join(common, string(filepath.Separator))
488	}
489	
490	// stripFileURI removes a leading file:// scheme and decodes escaped path bytes
491	// so URIs like file:///tmp/my%20file.go become /tmp/my file.go.
492	func stripFileURI(value string) string {
493		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(value)
494		if !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "file:") {
495			return trimmed
496		}
497		parsed, err := url.Parse(trimmed)
498		if err == nil && parsed.Scheme == "file" {
499			if decoded, err := url.PathUnescape(parsed.Path); err == nil {
500				return decoded
501			}
502			return parsed.Path
503		}
504		return strings.TrimPrefix(trimmed, "file://")
505	}

507	// msEpochToRFC3339 converts a millisecond epoch timestamp to an RFC3339 UTC
508	// string. Returns "" for non-positive input.
509	func msEpochToRFC3339(ms int64) string {
510		if ms <= 0 {
511			return ""
512		}
513		return time.UnixMilli(ms).UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
514	}

420	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every session in this provider's native store,
421	// regardless of project. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
422	//
423	// Gemini associates a tmp directory (~/.gemini/tmp/<hash>/) with a project via a
424	// .project_root marker file holding the project path, which is the originating cwd
425	// for every session in that directory.
426	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
427		tmpDir, err := GetGeminiTmpDir()
428		if err != nil {
429			return nil, err
430		}
431		entries, err := os.ReadDir(tmpDir)
432		if err != nil {
433			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
434				return []spi.GlobalSessionRef{}, nil
435			}
436			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read Gemini tmp directory: %w", err)
437		}
438	
439		var refs []spi.GlobalSessionRef
440		for _, entry := range entries {
441			if !entry.IsDir() {
442				continue
443			}
444			dir := filepath.Join(tmpDir, entry.Name())
445	
446			// The .project_root marker holds the project path — the originating cwd shared
447			// by every session in this tmp directory.
448			var cwd string
449			if content, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, ".project_root")); err == nil {
450				cwd = strings.TrimSpace(string(content))
451			}
452	
453			sessions, err := FindSessions(dir)
454			if err != nil {
455				slog.Debug("reindex: failed to find gemini sessions", "dir", dir, "error", err)
456				continue
457			}
458			for _, session := range sessions {
459				metadata := extractGeminiSessionMetadata(session)
460				if metadata == nil {
461					continue // empty session
462				}
463				refs = append(refs, spi.GlobalSessionRef{
464					SessionID:  metadata.SessionID,
465					CreatedAt:  metadata.CreatedAt,
466					Slug:       metadata.Slug,
467					Name:       metadata.Name,
468					NativePath: session.FilePath,
469					OriginCwd:  cwd,
470				})
471			}
472		}
473		return refs, nil
474	}

184		r.ensureInitialized()
185	
186		// Build the provider list only once and cache it
187		r.providerListOnce.Do(func() {
188			r.mu.RLock()
189			defer r.mu.RUnlock()

200			}
201			sort.Strings(ids)

205			for _, id := range ids {

208				}
209			}
210	
211			r.providerListCache = strings.Join(parts, ", ")
212		})
213	
214		return r.providerListCache
215	}

17	// ReconstructSession rebuilds a Gemini CLI native chat session from the neutral
18	// SessionData so `gemini --resume <id>` can continue the conversation.
19	//
20	// Gemini stores a session as a single JSON document: a top-level object with
21	// `sessionId`/`projectHash`/`startTime`/`lastUpdated`/`kind` and a `messages`
22	// array. Each message is `{id, timestamp, type, content}` where a user message's
23	// content is `[{text}]` and a gemini message's content is a plain string. Tool
24	// calls and thinking are already flattened into agent text by FlattenSessionData,
25	// so reconstruction emits only `user`/`gemini` text messages. See
26	// docs/SESSION-PORTABILITY.md.
27	func (p *Provider) ReconstructSession(data *schema.SessionData, opts spi.ReconstructOptions) (*spi.ReconstructedSession, error) {
28		turns, err := spi.PrepareTurns(data, opts)
29		if err != nil {
30			return nil, err
31		}
32		cwd := spi.ResolveWorkspaceRoot(opts, data)
33	
34		newID := uuid.NewString()
35		base := time.Now().UTC()
36	
37		// Best-effort project hash; Gemini stores it but resume keys off the project dir.
38		projectHash, _ := HashProjectPath(cwd)
39	
40		messages := make([]map[string]interface{}, 0, len(turns))
41		for i, turn := range turns {
42			msg := map[string]interface{}{
43				"id":        uuid.NewString(),
44				"timestamp": spi.RFC3339Millis(base.Add(time.Duration(i) * time.Second)),
45			}
46			if turn.Role == schema.RoleUser {
47				msg["type"] = "user"
48				msg["content"] = []map[string]interface{}{{"text": turn.Text}}
49			} else {
50				msg["type"] = "gemini"
51				msg["content"] = turn.Text
52			}
53			messages = append(messages, msg)
54		}
55	
56		session := map[string]interface{}{
57			"sessionId":   newID,
58			"projectHash": projectHash,
59			"startTime":   spi.RFC3339Millis(base),
60			"lastUpdated": spi.RFC3339Millis(base.Add(time.Duration(len(turns)) * time.Second)),
61			"kind":        "main",
62			"messages":    messages,
63			// Provenance back-link to the source session this was reconstructed from, so the
64			// lineage stays traceable (matches claude/codex/droid). See docs/SESSION-PORTABILITY.md.
65			"specstorySourceSessionId": data.SessionID,
66		}
67	
68		var buf bytes.Buffer
69		enc := json.NewEncoder(&buf)
70		enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
71		enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
72		if err := enc.Encode(session); err != nil {
73			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to encode gemini session: %w", err)
74		}
75	
76		// Filename: session-<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM>-<first 8 of id>.json (Gemini convention).
77		filename := fmt.Sprintf("session-%s-%s.json", base.Format("2006-01-02T15-04"), newID[:8])
78	
79		return &spi.ReconstructedSession{
80			SessionID: newID,
81			Filename:  filename,
82			Content:   buf.Bytes(),
83		}, nil
84	}
85	
86	// NativeSessionPath returns where a reconstructed chat belongs in Gemini's store
87	// and, unlike the Claude/Codex resolvers, prepares the project directory: Gemini
88	// associates a tmp dir with a project via a `.project_root` marker, so for a
89	// project Gemini has never seen we create `~/.gemini/tmp/<name>/` with that marker
90	// and a `chats/` subdir. Returns `<projectDir>/chats/<filename>`.
91	func (p *Provider) NativeSessionPath(projectPath string, filename string) (string, error) {
92		if projectPath == "" {
93			var err error
94			projectPath, err = osGetwd()
95			if err != nil {
96				return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get current working directory: %w", err)
97			}
98		}
99	
100		// Reuse the project dir Gemini already associates with this project, if any.
101		dir, err := ResolveGeminiProjectDir(projectPath)
102		if err != nil {
103			dir, err = prepareGeminiProjectDir(projectPath)
104			if err != nil {
105				return "", err
106			}
107		}
108	
109		return filepath.Join(dir, "chats", filename), nil
110	}
111	
112	// prepareGeminiProjectDir creates a Gemini project directory for a project that
113	// Gemini has not seen yet: ~/.gemini/tmp/<basename>/ (falling back to the hash dir
114	// if that basename is taken by a different project), with a `.project_root` marker
115	// and a `chats/` subdirectory.
116	func prepareGeminiProjectDir(projectPath string) (string, error) {
117		tmpDir, err := GetGeminiTmpDir()
118		if err != nil {
119			return "", err
120		}
121		if err := os.MkdirAll(tmpDir, 0o755); err != nil {
122			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to create gemini tmp dir: %w", err)
123		}
124	
125		canonical := canonicalizeProjectPath(projectPath)
126		dir := filepath.Join(tmpDir, filepath.Base(projectPath))
127	
128		// If the basename dir exists but belongs to a different project, key off the hash instead.
129		if info, statErr := osStat(dir); statErr == nil && info.IsDir() && !matchesProjectRoot(dir, canonical) {
130			if dir, err = GetGeminiProjectDir(projectPath); err != nil {
131				return "", err
132			}
133		}
134	
135		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(dir, "chats"), 0o755); err != nil {
136			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to create gemini chats dir: %w", err)
137		}
138	
139		// Write the project-root marker so Gemini maps this dir to the project on resume.
140		rootFile := filepath.Join(dir, ".project_root")
141		if _, statErr := osStat(rootFile); os.IsNotExist(statErr) {
142			if err := os.WriteFile(rootFile, []byte(canonical), 0o644); err != nil {
143				return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to write gemini .project_root: %w", err)
144			}
145		}
146	
147		return dir, nil
148	}
149

24	// expandTilde expands a leading ~ to the user's home directory so users can

26	func expandTilde(path string) string {
27		if !strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") {
28			return path
29		}
30		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
31		if err != nil {
32			return path
33		}

37	// parseCommand splits a custom command string into executable name and args,
38	// returning the default command when customCommand is empty.
39	func parseCommand(customCommand string) (string, []string) {
40		if strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != "" {
41			parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
42			if len(parts) > 0 {
43				return expandTilde(parts[0]), parts[1:]
44			}
45		}
46		return defaultCommand, nil
47	}

49	// ExecuteAntigravity launches the Antigravity CLI and blocks until it exits.
50	func ExecuteAntigravity(customCommand string, resumeSessionID string) error {
51		cmdName, args := parseCommand(customCommand)
52		args = ensureResumeArgs(args, resumeSessionID)
53		if resumeSessionID != "" {
54			slog.Info("ExecuteAntigravity: resuming conversation", "conversationId", resumeSessionID)
55		}
56	
57		command := exec.Command(cmdName, args...)
58		command.Stdin = os.Stdin
59		command.Stdout = os.Stdout
60		command.Stderr = os.Stderr
61	
62		return command.Run()
63	}

66	// caller already supplied a conversation flag with a value.
67	func ensureResumeArgs(args []string, resumeSessionID string) []string {
68		if resumeSessionID == "" {
69			return args
70		}
71	
72		for i, arg := range args {
73			if arg == resumeFlag {
74				if i+1 < len(args) && strings.TrimSpace(args[i+1]) != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(args[i+1], "-") {
75					return args
76				}
77				// slices.Concat always allocates a new backing array, so the caller's
78				// slice is never mutated.
79				return slices.Concat(args[:i+1], []string{resumeSessionID}, args[i+1:])
80			}
81			if strings.HasPrefix(arg, resumeFlag+"=") {
82				if strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(arg, resumeFlag+"=")) != "" {
83					return args
84				}
85				repaired := slices.Clone(args)
86				repaired[i] = resumeFlag + "=" + resumeSessionID
87				return repaired
88			}
89		}
90	
91		return append(args, resumeFlag, resumeSessionID)
92	}

I now have a complete, independently-verified picture. The conformance sweep is still running in the background to catch any remaining minor items, but I have enough to give you the substantive analysis. I'll fold in the sweep's polish findings when it lands.

## Antigravity CLI provider — readiness analysis

### The headline: it doesn't compile

The provider was written against an older SPI. Three interface methods added to `spi.Provider` since then are entirely absent, so the registry assignment fails:

```
pkg/spi/factory/registry.go:92: *antigravitycli.Provider does not implement spi.Provider (missing method ListAllAgentChatSessions)
```

`go build ./...` fails today. The compiler only names the first missing method, but all three are gone:

| Missing method | Purpose | Feasibility for Antigravity |
|---|---|---|
| `ListAllAgentChatSessions()` | Powers `specstory reindex` — enumerate every session across all projects, each carrying its origin cwd | **Feasible.** Walk `brain/<id>/`, reuse the existing `resolveSessionWorkspace` logic for `OriginCwd` |
| `ReconstructSession(data, opts)` | Rebuild a native session so the agent can resume it (reverse flow) | **Questionable** — see below |
| `NativeSessionPath(projectPath, filename)` | Where a reconstructed file belongs in the native store | Trivial once the reconstruct decision is made |

The good news: everything *else* is in solid shape. The parse/generate path (`agent_session.go`), workspace inference, `path_utils.go`, exec wrapper, watcher, config wiring, and README are all mature and correctly reuse shared SPI helpers (`spi.GetCanonicalPath`, `spi.SplitCommandLine`, `spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage`, `spi.GetDebugDir`). `SessionData` is fully populated, so cloud sync works. The Antigravity package compiles and vets cleanly on its own — only the interface conformance is broken.

### The one real design decision: reconstruction

# Antigravity CLI Provider Conformance Audit

## RELEASE-BLOCKING

### 1. The entire module does not compile — three SPI interface methods are missing

`pkg/providers/antigravitycli/` implements only 8 of the 11 methods on `spi.Provider` (`pkg/spi/provider.go:61-145`). Missing:

- **`NativeSessionPath(projectPath, filename string) (string, error)`** — `provider.go:136`
- **`ReconstructSession(data, opts) (*ReconstructedSession, error)`** — `provider.go:129`

Because of this, `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go:92` fails:

```
pkg/spi/factory/registry.go:92:31: cannot use antigravityProvider ... does not implement spi.Provider (missing method ListAllAgentChatSessions)
```

`go build ./...` exits 1. This is the **only** build error in the module, and it blocks everything. (Go stops at the first missing method, so only `ListAllAgentChatSessions` is named, but all three are absent.)

Note the trap: `go test ./pkg/providers/antigravitycli/` **passes** in isolation, because the package never asserts itself against `spi.Provider` internally (no provider uses a `var _ spi.Provider = (*Provider)(nil)` guard). The violation surfaces only when the factory imports it.

All 7 sibling providers implement `ListAllAgentChatSessions` — including the non-reconstructing ones (`deepseektui/provider.go:326`, `cursoride`, `cursorcli`). This method is **mandatory** on the interface; it is what `specstory reindex` calls for every registered provider via `registry.ListIDs()` → `prov.ListAllAgentChatSessions()` (`pkg/cmd/reindex.go:170,271`). Antigravity is registered under id `"antigravity"` (`registry.go:91-92`), so reindex will invoke it.

Reference patterns to follow:
- **`ReconstructSession` + `NativeSessionPath`**: `geminicli/reconstruct.go:27,91` (full worked example: `spi.PrepareTurns`, `spi.ResolveWorkspaceRoot`, `spi.RFC3339Millis`, native path prep). Also `droidcli/reconstruct.go`, `codexcli/reconstruct.go`, `claudecode/reconstruct.go`.
- No provider currently returns `spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported` — all four references produce real native output — but the SPI explicitly permits returning `ErrReconstructionUnsupported` (`pkg/spi/reconstruct.go:16`) as the minimum bar if a native serializer isn't ready. `NativeSessionPath` would then also return it.
- **`ListAllAgentChatSessions`**: `deepseektui/provider.go:326` is the closest structural match — antigravity's store is a `brain/<conversationID>/` directory tree (not one-`.jsonl`-per-session), so the parallel `spi.ScanSessionsInParallel` helper (`pkg/spi/global.go:93`, used by claude/codex) does not directly apply; deepseek's hand-rolled walk building `spi.GlobalSessionRef{...}` with `OriginCwd` is the right template.

### 2. `specstory resume antigravity` cannot work

Don't reach for `spi.ScanSessionsInParallel` (the helper claude/codex use) — that walks a flat `*.jsonl` tree. Antigravity's store is a `brain/<conversationID>/.system_generated/logs/transcript_full.jsonl` **directory tree**, so the right template is **`deepseektui/provider.go:326`**: a hand-rolled walk that builds each `spi.GlobalSessionRef` with `OriginCwd`. The good news — the hard part is already written: `resolveSessionWorkspace` (`agent_session.go:354`) already resolves the origin cwd via history.jsonl → CLI-log/config join → tool-path inference, exactly what `OriginCwd` needs. - If the encrypted `.pb` is load-bearing → reconstruction is genuinely infeasible, and the honest implementation is `ReconstructSession`/`NativeSessionPath` returning `spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported`. The SPI explicitly permits this (`reconstruct.go:16`); no current provider uses it, but that's the intended fallback. Either way, the method must *exist* to compile.

## Spike result: transcript-only resume does **not** work

The experiment is conclusive. `agy` 1.1.3 rebuilds conversation context exclusively from the **protobuf-in-SQLite `conversations/<id>.db`**. The `transcript_full.jsonl` is a write-only log that resume never reads:

- **Remove the `.db`, keep the transcript** → `agy` resumes with *zero* memory. It didn't know the secret and started searching the filesystem for it. The transcript sitting right there was ignored.
- **Remove the transcript, keep the `.db`** → perfect recall. Resume doesn't need the transcript at all.

And your original confound is fully retired: **there is no encrypted `.pb` in 1.1.3** — no `.pb` files, no `implicit/` dir. The 1.0.2 encrypted blob was replaced by this *readable* protobuf-in-SQLite store (I can `grep` the plaintext secret straight out of the `.db`).

### What this means for `ReconstructSession`

The simple serializer path that Gemini/Droid/Codex use — write a flattened transcript in the native text format — is a **dead end for Antigravity**. Writing a synthetic `transcript_full.jsonl` produces a file `agy` will never load. To make a reconstructed session actually resumable, we'd have to synthesize the **SQLite `.db` with valid protobuf `step_payload`s** matching `agy`'s internal schema (`steps`, `gen_metadata`, `trajectory_meta`, `trajectory_metadata_blob`, …). That's a materially harder and more version-brittle target than any existing provider's serializer — the payloads are raw protobuf with no `.proto` in hand, so it'd mean reverse-engineering the message schema and tracking it across `agy` releases.

So the reconstruct decision is now a real fork, and I'd frame it as:

1. **Ship `ErrReconstructionUnsupported` for v1 (my recommendation).** The SPI explicitly permits it (`reconstruct.go:16`). Honest, unblocks the build immediately, and Antigravity still gets full forward support (parse → markdown → cloud sync) and `reindex` via `ListAllAgentChatSessions`. Only cross-agent *resume-into-Antigravity* is deferred.
2. **Invest in a protobuf-SQLite serializer.** Real resume, but a significant reverse-engineering effort with ongoing version-fragility risk. Worth a separate spike to scope the protobuf schema before committing.

Two secondary findings worth logging:

- **The format spec is now partially stale for 1.1.3.** `docs/antigravity-format-spec.md` §1 describes the conversation store as an encrypted `.pb`; it's now a readable SQLite DB. I also saw a new `CHECKPOINT` step type in the transcript (conversation truncation marker) that isn't in the spec's §3.2 enum. The *parser* still works (it reads the transcript, which is unchanged in shape), but the doc should be updated.
- Your `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/` now has a few throwaway test sessions from this spike (secrets PURPLE-ELEPHANT / ORANGE-TIGER). Harmless, but say the word and I'll delete those brain dirs + `.db`s.

Confirmed the specifics. Here's the consolidated standing.

## Where we stand — Antigravity CLI provider

### Decisions locked
- **Reconstruct:** `ReconstructSession` + `NativeSessionPath` → return `spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported`. The spike proved resume reads the protobuf-SQLite `.db`, not the transcript, so a transcript serializer would be a broken promise. A real serializer would mean reverse-engineering `agy`'s protobuf step schema — deferred, not in v1.

### Release blockers (the build is red until these land)
| # | Item | Effort | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ListAllAgentChatSessions()` — real impl | Medium | deepseek-style walk of `brain/<id>/` dirs; `OriginCwd` comes free from the existing `resolveSessionWorkspace`. This is the one that needs actual logic. |
| 2 | `ReconstructSession()` → `ErrReconstructionUnsupported` | Trivial | Decided. |
| 3 | `NativeSessionPath()` → `ErrReconstructionUnsupported` | Trivial | Pairs with #2. |
| 4 | `var _ spi.Provider = (*Provider)(nil)` compile guard | Trivial | So this class of drift fails at the package, not just the factory. No provider currently has one — worth adding here. |

### 1.1.3 transition learnings — the newly-surfaced work
These are things the spike exposed that weren't visible when the provider was written against 1.0.2:

1. **The provider has never run end-to-end.** Because the build is broken, `specstory sync antigravity` has *never executed* against a real capture. Its tests pass, but all fixtures are inline strings hand-derived from the 1.0.2 spec — the suite has never seen 1.1.3 output. **Silver lining:** I just created real 1.1.3 sessions on disk. The moment it compiles, we can run the actual provider against them and eyeball the markdown — the first true validation.

2. **New `CHECKPOINT` step type is silently dropped.** 1.1.3 emits `type: "CHECKPOINT"` (a conversation-truncation marker) that the 1.0.2 spec never listed. `buildExchanges` has no constant for it, so it falls to the `default:` case and is skipped with a debug log. Functionally safe (it's not user content), but it deserves an explicit `typeCheckpoint` const + a deliberate "skip" with a test, rather than landing in the catch-all by accident.

3. **The format spec doc is stale.** `docs/antigravity-format-spec.md` §1 still describes `conversations/<id>.pb` as an *encrypted* blob and §3.2's type enum omits `CHECKPOINT`. Reality in 1.1.3: it's a readable protobuf-in-SQLite `.db` (no `.pb`, no `implicit/` dir), plus the checkpoint type. Doc-only, but it's now misleading.

4. **Richer metadata is newly available (enhancement, not a gap).** 1.1.3 added a top-level `conversation_summaries.db` and per-conversation `.db`s that likely carry real session names/summaries — a better source for `SessionMetadata.Name` / `GlobalSessionRef.Name` than the current first-prompt derivation. Also worth knowing: a `.db` can exist with no `brain/` dir (I saw a stray sub-trajectory), which confirms **`brain/`-dir enumeration is the correct scoping** for `ListAllAgentChatSessions` (only those have parseable transcripts).

1	# Antigravity CLI — On-Disk Session Storage Format Spec
2	
3	Authoritative, reverse-engineered specification of how Google's **Antigravity
4	agentic coding CLI** (`agy` binary) stores sessions on disk. Intended for an
5	engineer writing a Go parser. Every claim below is backed by real captured data
6	observed on macOS.
7	
8	- App: `agy` on `PATH` (for example, `~/.local/bin/agy`)
9	- Versions observed: `1.0.2` (original capture) and `1.1.3` (re-validation)
10	- App data root: `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/`
11	- Capture dates: 2026-05-26 (`1.0.2`), 2026-07-21 (`1.1.3`)
12	
13	> **1.1.3 storage-format change (READ FIRST).** Between `1.0.2` and `1.1.3` the
14	> per-conversation store changed shape. The encrypted `conversations/<id>.pb`
15	> blob and the `implicit/<uuid>.pb` files are **gone**; conversations are now a
16	> **readable SQLite database** at `conversations/<id>.db` (see §1.1). The
17	> plaintext `brain/<id>/…/transcript_full.jsonl` transcript is unchanged in
18	> shape and remains the source a parser reads. Two additions also appear in
19	> `1.1.3`: a `CHECKPOINT` transcript step type (§3.2) and a top-level
20	> `conversation_summaries.db`. **Resume reads the SQLite store, not the
21	> transcript** (see §1.1) — a fact with direct consequences for session
22	> reconstruction.
23	- Scenarios used for this spec (captured on disk at the time of analysis):
24	  - interactive TUI session, 11 steps, all `run_command`
25	  - `agy -p "say hello"`, 3 steps, no tools (text-only)

27	  - `agy -p --add-dir`, file tools `view_file`/`write_to_file`/`grep_search`/`list_dir`
28	  - `agy -p --add-dir` edit + failing command, then `agy -c` continuation (multi-turn, append-only)

290			Slug:      slug,
291			Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(prompt),
292		}

295	// firstUserPromptText returns the cleaned text of the first USER_INPUT step that
296	// carries a real prompt, or "" if none.
297	func firstUserPromptText(session *agSession) string {
298		for _, step := range session.Steps {
299			if step.Type != typeUserInput {
300				continue
301			}
302			if text := cleanUserPrompt(step.Content); text != "" {
303				return text

```go
package antigravitycli

import (
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

// Compile-time assertion that Provider satisfies the full spi.Provider contract.
// The interface conformance is otherwise only exercised at registration in the
// factory package, so a locally missing method fails there rather than here;
// this guard surfaces the gap in the provider's own package.
var _ spi.Provider = (*Provider)(nil)

// ReconstructSession is unsupported for Antigravity. On resume, `agy` rebuilds
// conversation state from the per-conversation SQLite store
// (conversations/<id>.db, protobuf step payloads) — NOT from the plaintext
// transcript this provider parses (verified empirically; see
// docs/antigravity-format-spec.md §1.1). A resumable reconstruction would
// therefore have to synthesize that protobuf-in-SQLite store, so the
// text-serializer approach the other providers use cannot produce a session
// `agy` will actually resume. Until such a serializer exists, this provider
// carries the interface method but declines to reconstruct.
func (p *Provider) ReconstructSession(data *schema.SessionData, opts spi.ReconstructOptions) (*spi.ReconstructedSession, error) {
	return nil, spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported
}

// NativeSessionPath is unsupported for the same reason as ReconstructSession:
// there is no plaintext session file this provider can write that `agy` would
// resume from, so there is no native path to resolve.
func (p *Provider) NativeSessionPath(projectPath string, filename string) (string, error) {
	return "", spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported
}

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-21 21:45:41Z)**_

Fixed. Root cause and fix:

**Root cause:** `agentTag` padded agent ids with `%-8s`. `antigravity` is 11 chars, so it overflowed the 8-column field and pushed the time, prompt, and count columns 3 columns right on that row — exactly the misalignment in your screenshot.

**Fix:** The agent column is now dynamically sized to the longest known agent id (`agentColWidth()`, floored at 8). Every tag pads to that same width, so columns line up across rows regardless of name length. I also shrank the label budget by the extra width in all four row paths — `sessionRow` dense/sparse and `globalRow` dense/sparse — so the right-hand turns/count column can't get shoved toward (or off) the edge.

The floor-at-8 means any install *without* antigravity renders identically to before — no regression for the shorter-name case.

Build ✅ · lint 0 issues ✅ · `pkg/cmd` tests pass ✅.

Worth an eyeball in the actual TUI to confirm it looks right — the columns should now align between the `claude` and `antigravity` rows, with the prompt text and the trailing `2`/`1` counts flush. If you want the agent column to have a bit more breathing room (an extra space of gutter after the widest name), I can bump the floor/padding — but as-is it aligns tightly.

// loadTaskOutputs reads optional async command logs from
// .system_generated/tasks/task-<step_index>.log. Antigravity names the task log
// after the RUN_COMMAND result step that remains RUNNING in the transcript.
func loadTaskOutputs(transcriptPath string) (map[int]string, error) {
	systemDir := filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(transcriptPath))
	tasksDir := filepath.Join(systemDir, "tasks")
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(tasksDir)
	if err != nil {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return nil, nil
		}
		return nil, err
	}

	outputs := make(map[int]string)
	for _, entry := range entries {
		if entry.IsDir() {
			continue
		}
		name := entry.Name()
		if !strings.HasPrefix(name, "task-") || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".log") {
			continue
		}

Both done. Here's where things land.

## Tests for the three new SPI methods — done

- **`reconstruct_test.go`** (new): `TestReconstructSession_Unsupported` and `TestNativeSessionPath_Unsupported` assert both return `ErrReconstructionUnsupported` (nil/empty result). This also restores the conventional `reconstruct_test.go` every sibling ships.
- **`TestListAllAgentChatSessions`** (in `provider_test.go`): builds a temp brain tree with a workspace-scoped session (workspace via `history.jsonl` → asserts `OriginCwd`) and a text-only session (asserts empty `OriginCwd` but still enumerated), verifying `SessionID`/`NativePath`/`Slug`.

All three pass; full antigravity suite green; lint 0 issues.

## `conversation_summaries.db` for a better Name source — investigated

It's a single-table SQLite DB keyed by `conversation_id`, and richer than expected:

| Column | Value in my capture | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `preview` | `"Store Secret Passphrase"` | A clean generated title — **better than our first-prompt slug** |
| `title` | *(empty)* | Intended title, but populated lazily/async |
| `workspace_uris` | *(empty — no `--add-dir`)* | Would carry the workspace for scoped sessions → **better than tool-path inference** |
| `project_id` | `"default-cli-project"` | Antigravity's own project handle |
| `step_count`, `last_modified_time`, `agent_name`, `parent_conversation_id`, `nesting_depth` | populated | metadata |

**Two findings that shape the recommendation:**

1. **It's a genuine upgrade for `Name` and potentially `WorkspaceRoot`.** `preview`/`title` beat the derived slug, and `workspace_uris`/`project_id` could fix the provider's weakest area — workspace resolution for print-mode sessions (currently heuristic tool-path common-prefix inference, spec §5.3).
2. **But coverage is partial and async.** Only **1 of 3+** on-disk conversations was indexed, and even that row had `title` empty while `preview` was set. So it **cannot be the source of truth** — only a best-effort overlay with fallback to the current logic.

**Cost is low:** `modernc.org/sqlite` (pure-Go, no cgo) is **already a dependency** — the Cursor providers use it — so reading this adds no new dependency, just a SQLite read + a small enrichment/merge layer.

**Recommendation:** worth doing as a **post-v1 enhancement**, not a blocker. Wire it as an optional overlay: prefer `title` → `preview` for `Name` (fall back to first-prompt derivation), and optionally promote `workspace_uris`/`project_id` above tool-path inference for workspace resolution. Because it's partial/async, it must degrade gracefully when a row is missing. The current first-prompt Name is perfectly serviceable for shipping now.

---

**Net status:** the provider is functionally complete and test-covered for v1 — build green, all three previously-untested SPI methods now covered, forward path validated, docs/changelog accurate, reconstruct decided-and-tested. The summaries-DB enrichment is the one clear future improvement on the table. Want me to file it somewhere (changelog "future"/a TODO), or leave it in your hands with your deeper-validation pass?

18	// BlobRecord represents a raw blob from the Cursor SQLite database
19	type BlobRecord struct {
20		RowID int             `json:"rowid"`
21		ID    string          `json:"id"`
22		Data  json.RawMessage `json:"data"` // Keep as raw JSON to preserve structure
23	}
24	
25	// extractFirstUserMessage extracts the full text of the first suitable user message
26	// Returns empty string if no suitable message is found
27	func extractFirstUserMessage(blobRecords []BlobRecord) string {
28		for _, record := range blobRecords {
29			// Try to parse the data to check role and content
30			var data struct {
31				Role    string `json:"role"`
32				Content []struct {
33					Type string `json:"type"`
34					Text string `json:"text"`
35				} `json:"content"`
36			}
37	
38			if err := json.Unmarshal(record.Data, &data); err != nil {
39				continue // Skip if can't parse
40			}
41	
42			// Check if this is a user message
43			if data.Role != "user" {
44				continue
45			}
46	
47			// Check if we have content with text
48			if len(data.Content) == 0 || data.Content[0].Type != "text" {
49				continue
50			}
51	
52			text := data.Content[0].Text
53	
54			// Strip <user_query> tags if present
55			text = stripUserQueryTags(text)
56	
57			// Skip if starts with <user_info> (may be JSON-encoded as \u003cuser_info\u003e)
58			if strings.HasPrefix(text, "<user_info>") || strings.HasPrefix(text, "\u003cuser_info\u003e") {
59				continue
60			}
61	
62			// Return the full text
63			if strings.TrimSpace(text) != "" {
64				return text
65			}
66		}
67	
68		return ""
69	}
70	
71	// extractSlugFromBlobs extracts a slug from the first suitable user message
72	func extractSlugFromBlobs(blobRecords []BlobRecord) string {
73		text := extractFirstUserMessage(blobRecords)
74		if text == "" {
75			slog.Debug("No suitable user message found for slug extraction")
76			return ""
77		}
78		slug := spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(text)
79		slog.Debug("Extracted slug from user message", "slug", slug)
80		return slug

83	// validateCursorDatabase validates that the SQLite database has the expected Cursor schema.
84	// This ensures we're working with a genuine Cursor database and not some other SQLite file.
85	func validateCursorDatabase(db *sql.DB) error {
86		// Define the expected schema for a Cursor database
87		type tableSchema struct {
88			name    string
89			columns []string // Required columns
90		}
91	
92		requiredTables := []tableSchema{
93			{
94				name:    "blobs",
95				columns: []string{"id", "data"},
96			},
97			{
98				name:    "meta",
99				columns: []string{"key", "value"},
100			},
101		}
102	
103		// Validate each required table exists and has expected columns
104		for _, table := range requiredTables {
105			// Check if table exists
106			var tableExists int
107			err := db.QueryRow(
108				"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name=?",
109				table.name,
110			).Scan(&tableExists)
111			if err != nil {
112				return fmt.Errorf("failed to check for table %s: %w", table.name, err)
113			}
114			if tableExists == 0 {
115				return fmt.Errorf("invalid Cursor database: missing required table '%s'", table.name)
116			}
117	
118			// Validate columns exist in the table
119			// Note: pragma_table_info doesn't support parameter binding, so we use fmt.Sprintf
120			// This is safe because table.name comes from our hardcoded schema, not user input
121			for _, column := range table.columns {
122				var columnExists int
123				query := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_table_info('%s') WHERE name=?", table.name)
124				err := db.QueryRow(query, column).Scan(&columnExists)
125				if err != nil {
126					return fmt.Errorf("failed to check column %s.%s: %w", table.name, column, err)
127				}
128				if columnExists == 0 {
129					return fmt.Errorf("invalid Cursor database: table '%s' missing required column '%s'", table.name, column)
130				}
131			}
132		}
133	
134		slog.Debug("Database schema validation passed")
135		return nil
136	}

138	// getSessionTimestamp retrieves the session creation timestamp from the meta table
139	func getSessionTimestamp(db *sql.DB) (string, error) {
140		var rawValue string
141		err := db.QueryRow("SELECT value FROM meta WHERE key='0'").Scan(&rawValue)
142		if err != nil {
143			slog.Debug("Failed to get metadata from meta table", "error", err)
144			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get metadata: %w", err)
145		}
146	
147		// The value is hex-encoded
148		jsonBytes, err := hex.DecodeString(rawValue)
149		if err != nil {
150			slog.Debug("Failed to decode hex metadata", "error", err)
151			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to decode hex: %w", err)
152		}
153	
154		// Parse the JSON
155		var metadata struct {
156			CreatedAt int64 `json:"createdAt"`
157		}
158		if err := json.Unmarshal(jsonBytes, &metadata); err != nil {
159			slog.Debug("Failed to parse metadata JSON", "error", err)
160			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to parse metadata: %w", err)
161		}
162	
163		slog.Debug("Found createdAt in metadata", "createdAt", metadata.CreatedAt)
164	
165		if metadata.CreatedAt > 0 {
166			// Convert milliseconds to time
167			ts := time.Unix(metadata.CreatedAt/1000, (metadata.CreatedAt%1000)*1000000)
168			slog.Debug("Converted timestamp", "timestamp", ts)
169			// Return as ISO 8601 format
170			return ts.Format(time.RFC3339), nil
171		}
172	
173		// Return current time as fallback
174		return time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339), nil
175	}
176	
177	// ReadSessionData reads all blobs from a Cursor session's store.db file
178	// Returns the creation timestamp, slug, blob records in topologically sorted order, and orphaned blobs
179	func ReadSessionData(sessionPath string) (string, string, []BlobRecord, []BlobRecord, error) {
180		dbPath := filepath.Join(sessionPath, "store.db")
181	
182		slog.Debug("Opening Cursor CLI SQLite database", "path", dbPath)
183	
184		// Open the database in read-only mode
185		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", dbPath+"?mode=ro")
186		if err != nil {
187			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open database: %w", err)
188		}
189		defer func() {
190			if err := db.Close(); err != nil {
191				slog.Debug("Failed to close database", "error", err)
192			}
193		}()
194	
195		slog.Debug("Successfully opened database", "path", dbPath)
196	
197		// Enable WAL mode for non-blocking reads
198		// This prevents readers from blocking the cursor-agent writer
199		if _, err := db.Exec("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL"); err != nil {
200			// Log warning but continue - not fatal if WAL fails
201			slog.Warn("Failed to enable WAL mode", "error", err)
202		} else {
203			slog.Debug("Enabled WAL mode for non-blocking reads")
204		}
205	
206		// Validate that this is actually a Cursor database with the expected schema
207		if err := validateCursorDatabase(db); err != nil {
208			return "", "", nil, nil, err
209		}
210	
211		// Get the session timestamp from metadata
212		createdAt, err := getSessionTimestamp(db)
213		if err != nil {
214			// Log but don't fail - use current time as fallback
215			slog.Debug("Failed to get session timestamp, using current time", "error", err)
216			createdAt = time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339)
217		}
218	
219		// Query all blobs
220		rows, err := db.Query("SELECT rowid, id, data FROM blobs")
221		if err != nil {
222			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to query blobs: %w", err)
223		}
224		defer func() {
225			if err := rows.Close(); err != nil {
226				slog.Debug("Failed to close rows", "error", err)
227			}
228		}()
229	
230		// Count total blobs for logging
231		var totalBlobs, jsonBlobs, skippedBlobs int
232	
233		slog.Debug("Starting to process blobs from database")
234	
235		// Collect all blobs and build a map for sorting
236		blobMap := make(map[string]*CursorBlob)
237		var allRowIDs []int // Collect all rowids for debugging
238	
239		for rows.Next() {
240			var rowid int
241			var id string
242			var data []byte
243	
244			totalBlobs++
245	
246			if err := rows.Scan(&rowid, &id, &data); err != nil {
247				slog.Debug("Failed to scan row", "error", err)
248				continue // Skip problematic rows
249			}
250	
251			// Collect rowid for debugging
252			allRowIDs = append(allRowIDs, rowid)
253	
254			// Log every single blob we process
255			idDisplay := id
256			if len(idDisplay) > 16 {
257				idDisplay = idDisplay[:16] + "..."
258			}
259			slog.Debug("Processing blob",
260				"rowid", rowid,
261				"id", idDisplay,
262				"data_len", len(data))
263	
264			// Parse references from the binary data
265			references := parseReferences(data, id, rowid)
266	
267			// Try to extract JSON from the binary data
268			jsonData := extractJSONFromBinary(data)
269			if jsonData != nil {
270				jsonBlobs++
271				blobMap[id] = &CursorBlob{
272					RowID:      rowid,
273					ID:         id,
274					Data:       json.RawMessage(jsonData),
275					RawData:    data,
276					References: references,
277				}
278			} else {
279				// If no JSON found, skip for now
280				// We may want to include these as reference-only blobs in the future
281				skippedBlobs++
282				// Uncomment this to see JSON detection in action when debugging the sqlite reader
283				idDisplay := id
284				if len(idDisplay) > 16 {
285					idDisplay = idDisplay[:16] + "..."
286				}
287				slog.Debug("Skipping blob (no JSON content found)",
288					"blob_id", idDisplay,
289					"rowid", rowid,
290					"has_references", len(references) > 0,
291					"reference_count", len(references))
292			}
293		}
294	
295		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
296			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("error iterating rows: %w", err)
297		}
298	
299		// Sort rowids for easier debugging
300		sort.Ints(allRowIDs)
301	
302		// Log all rowids we got from the database - check if 1555-1560 are present
303		slog.Debug("All rowids from database query",
304			"count", len(allRowIDs),
305			"min", allRowIDs[0],
306			"max", allRowIDs[len(allRowIDs)-1],
307			"rowids", allRowIDs)
308	
309		slog.Debug("Blob processing summary",
310			"totalBlobs", totalBlobs,
311			"jsonBlobs", jsonBlobs,
312			"skippedBlobs", skippedBlobs)
313	
314		// Perform topological sort on the blobs
315		sortedBlobs, orphanedBlobs, err := topologicalSort(blobMap)
316		if err != nil {
317			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to sort blobs: %w", err)
318		}
319	
320		// Convert sorted blobs to BlobRecord array (without References and RawData)
321		var blobRecords []BlobRecord
322		for _, blob := range sortedBlobs {
323			blobRecords = append(blobRecords, BlobRecord{
324				RowID: blob.RowID,
325				ID:    blob.ID,
326				Data:  blob.Data,
327			})
328		}
329	
330		// Convert orphaned blobs to BlobRecord array
331		var orphanRecords []BlobRecord
332		var orphanRowIDs []int
333		for _, blob := range orphanedBlobs {
334			orphanRecords = append(orphanRecords, BlobRecord{
335				RowID: blob.RowID,
336				ID:    blob.ID,
337				Data:  blob.Data,
338			})
339			orphanRowIDs = append(orphanRowIDs, blob.RowID)
340		}
341	
342		if len(orphanRowIDs) > 0 {
343			sort.Ints(orphanRowIDs)
344			slog.Debug("Orphaned blob rowids", "rowids", orphanRowIDs, "count", len(orphanRowIDs))
345		}
346	
347		// Log final DAG rowids before markdown generation
348		slog.Debug("Final DAG-sorted blob rowids before markdown generation:")
349		var rowids []int
350		for _, blob := range blobRecords {
351			rowids = append(rowids, blob.RowID)
352		}
353		slog.Debug("DAG rowids", "rowids", rowids, "count", len(rowids))
354	
355		// Extract slug from the final blob records
356		slug := extractSlugFromBlobs(blobRecords)
357	
358		return createdAt, slug, blobRecords, orphanRecords, nil
359	}
360	
361	// min returns the minimum of two integers
362	func min(a, b int) int {
363		if a < b {
364			return a
365		}
366		return b
367	}
368

64	func loadProjectWorkspaceIndex() (map[string]string, error) {
65		dir, err := resolveGeminiProjectsDir()
66		if err != nil {
67			return nil, err
68		}
69		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
70		if err != nil {

78		for _, entry := range entries {
79			if entry.IsDir() || filepath.Ext(entry.Name()) != ".json" {
80				continue
81			}
82			path := filepath.Join(dir, entry.Name())
83			data, err := os.ReadFile(path)

96			}
97			workspace := projectWorkspacePath(project)

99				continue
100			}
101			index[id] = workspace
102		}

104	}

179	func indexConversationProjectsFromLog(path string, index map[string]string) error {
180		f, err := os.Open(path)
181		if err != nil {
182			return err
183		}
184		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
185	
186		var currentProjectID string
187		var pendingConversationIDs []string
188		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(f)
189		scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64*1024), maxTranscriptLineSize)
190		for scanner.Scan() {
191			line := scanner.Text()
192			if projectID := projectIDFromLogLine(line); projectID != "" {
193				currentProjectID = projectID
194				for _, conversationID := range pendingConversationIDs {
195					index[conversationID] = currentProjectID
196				}
197				pendingConversationIDs = nil
198			}
199			for _, conversationID := range conversationIDsFromLogLine(line) {
200				if currentProjectID == "" {
201					pendingConversationIDs = append(pendingConversationIDs, conversationID)
202					continue
203				}
204				index[conversationID] = currentProjectID
205			}
206		}
207		if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
208			return err
209		}
210		return nil
211	}
212	
213	func projectIDFromLogLine(line string) string {
214		for _, re := range []*regexp.Regexp{projectIDFromConversationRe, projectIDFromUsingRe} {
215			if m := re.FindStringSubmatch(line); len(m) == 2 {
216				return strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(m[1]))
217			}
218		}
219		return ""
220	}
221	
222	func conversationIDsFromLogLine(line string) []string {
223		var ids []string
224		seen := make(map[string]bool)
225		for _, re := range conversationIDLogRes {
226			for _, m := range re.FindAllStringSubmatch(line, -1) {
227				if len(m) != 2 {
228					continue
229				}
230				id := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(m[1]))
231				if id == "" || seen[id] {
232					continue
233				}
234				seen[id] = true
235				ids = append(ids, id)
236			}
237		}
238		return ids
239	}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-21 22:10:09Z)**_

Done. Best-effort Name enrichment from `conversation_summaries.db` is implemented and tested.

## What changed

**`project_mapping.go`** (no new file, no new dependency — `modernc.org/sqlite` was already in the tree via the Cursor providers):
- `conversationSummary{Title, Preview}` + `bestName()` → prefers `title`, falls back to `preview`.
- `loadConversationSummaryIndex()` — reads `conversation_summaries.db` **read-only** (`?mode=ro` + WAL, so a live `agy` never blocks). Fully best-effort: missing file, missing table, or a bad row all degrade to an empty index rather than erroring.

**`sessionMetadata` (`transcript_parser.go`)** now resolves the Name as: summary `title` → summary `preview` → **existing prompt-derived readable name**. The map lookup is nil-safe (a missing conversation or nil index yields `""`, which triggers the fallback), so nothing breaks when the DB is absent.

**Wiring** — both `ListAgentChatSessions` and `ListAllAgentChatSessions` load the summaries index once and pass it through, so improved names flow to the listings, the resume TUI, and `reindex`/`GlobalSessionRef.Name`. Slug is untouched (still prompt-derived) — only the display Name is enriched, exactly as you scoped it.

## Tests
- `TestListAgentChatSessions_PrefersSummaryName` covers all three paths: title preferred, preview-when-title-empty, and derived fallback when there's no summary row. New `writeConversationSummary` fixture helper builds a real SQLite DB.
- Existing `sessionMetadata` direct-call tests updated for the new signature.

**Verification:** full module tests pass · whole-repo lint 0 issues · build OK. The live-DB schema (`conversation_id`/`title`/`preview`) matches exactly what the loader queries, confirmed against the real file earlier.

Since Antigravity populates this store asynchronously, expect the improved names to show up for older/settled sessions and the prompt-derived name for very fresh ones — which is the intended graceful behavior. Your deeper-validation pass is a good place to eyeball whether the summary titles read better than the derived ones in practice.

1	# SpecStory CLI Multi-Agent, Multi-Tool Test and Regressions
2	
3	This repository helps us understand the relationship between the various coding agents and the SpecStory CLI, particularly as it pertains to tool use.
4	
5	We use this repository, in particular, changes in the files contained here as an indication of changes:
6	- New versions of the coding agents are released
7	- New versions of the SpecStory CLI are released
8	
9	## Repo Organization
10	
11	There is a top-level directory per coding agent supported by the SpecStory CLI.
12	
13	Currently:
14	
15	- claude-code
16	- codex-cli
17	- gemini-cli
18	- cursor-cli
19	- droid-factory
20	- deepseek-tui
21	- antigravity
22	
23	Still to come:
24	
25	- cursor-ide
26	- copilot-ide
27	- amp
28	- opencode
29	- pi
30	
31	Within each agent top-level dir, there are dated folders for the date a new test is run. In this directory:
32	
33	- `versions.txt` - The coding agent version and SpecStory CLI version used for the test
34	- `.specstory/history/{specstory-history-file}.md` - the SpecStory CLI output for the tested session
35	- `.specstory/debug` - the SpecStory CLI raw session debug data
36	- `tool-use-audit.md` - agent report on the tool use formatting for the session
37	
38	
39	## Prompt Strategy
40	
41	The general prompting strategy is to run the coding agent directly (not via `specstory run`) and get it to enumurate, then use all of its available tools:
42	
43	```
44	Hello <agent>, tell me all the tools you have access to. Write all the tool names to the file `./tools.txt`.
45	
46	Please use each of your <number> tools one-by-one to show me how they work and how you use them.
47	
48	Please use your tool <tool-name> to show me how it works.
49	
50	Please use your <tool-name> tool to ...
51	```
52	
53	## Output Steps
54	
55	Run the specific version of SpecStory you want to test the output from in the date specific testing directory where the agent coding session was performed (see above):
56	
57	```zsh
58	specstory sync --log --debug --debug-raw
59	```
60	
61	Be sure to commit the `.specstory` directory that's output as that's the key to being able to compare the session output.
62	
63	## Finding and Fixing Issues
64	
65	Then ask an agent to examine the resulting session history file and flag unformatted (or poorly formatted) tool support. Here's a suggested prompt:
66	
67	```
68	Your task is to analyze the SpecStory CLI session output file: @<dir>/.specstory/history/<session>.md 
69	
70	This is a markdown representation of the session data here: @<dir>/.specstory/debug/
71	
72	We need an audit of the `tool-use` sections of the markdown against the raw data of the tool use. Make a qualitative assessment for each tool use that indicates if all the important data for the tool use is present and pleasantly presented for a human reader (✅ formatted), or there and formatted but missing important elements (😢 partial), there as raw JSON or otherwise unformatted output (🆘 raw/unformatted), or missing entirely (🚫 missing).
73	
74	Create a report in markdown at @<dir>/tool-use-audit.md with a table characterizing the quality of the output. Include these columns:
75	
76	- tool name
77	- md line number
78	- quality - ✅ formatted, 😢 partial, 🆘 raw/unformatted,  🚫 missing
79	- data file
80	- data line number
81	- comment
82	```
83
```
</details></tool-use>
